message.content: I have a question on the appointments-edges.test.ts. Why are we adding more original tests if in theory they've added it?

content.text:
Their suite does not cover everything, and the README says so: "The suite is a safety net, not a full specification. Plenty of the code isn't covered." The six tests cover gaps in it that this refactor could break. They do not repeat any test the reviewers wrote.

## What their suite leaves open

Each of these is behaviour the old code had, that their suite never checks, and that a rewrite changes easily:

| Behaviour | Their suite | What a rewrite does by default |
|---|---|---|
| `PATCH` of an unknown id with an invalid body returns 404 | Tests each case alone, never both together | Parses the body first and returns 400 |
| Empty notes are stored as `null` | Never sends empty notes | Stores `''` |
| An unknown `status` filter returns 200 with an empty list | Tests only `confirmed` | A schema with four statuses returns 400 |
| `GET /appointments/abc` returns 404 | Tests only `999` | A schema on the id returns 400 |
| An empty `status=` means no filter | Not tested | Can filter on `''` and return nothing |
| A legacy appointment returns its stored values | Skips legacy rows on purpose | Can normalise too early |

Without these tests, the refactor could change any of the six and the suite would stay green. The first two did shape the new code.

## Are they required

No. The brief asks you to keep their suite green, and it does not ask for more characterization tests. They are a choice, and the choice has two sides:

- **For:** the reviewers look first at "whether you protected existing behaviour" and at "whether your tests would catch a real regression".
- **Against:** they add a file to review, and the legacy test must change again in tickets 05 and 06.

## Recommendation

Keep the first four. They guard decisions you can explain in one sentence each in the walkthrough.

The last two are weaker: the empty filter is a minor case, and the legacy test records values that you plan to change. Removing them makes the file smaller and avoids two later edits. If you want that, tell me and I cut them, or delete the two `it` blocks yourself before you commit.

content.text:
Ticket 03, "Appointments web through the contract", is implemented and its two reviews are running; nothing is committed, so hold the commits until they report.

## What is done

| Item | Result |
|---|---|
| API client | `apps/web/lib/api.ts` is the only file that calls the API. It reads `API_URL` and `API_KEY`, which are server-only. |
| BFF handlers | All five use the client. The hardcoded URL and `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` are gone from the code and from `.env.example`. |
| Overview page | It calls a new BFF route, `/api/appointments/summary`, and no longer calls the API from the browser. |
| Page types | The appointments page, the confirmation page and the Overview take their types from the contract. No `any` remains in them. |
| BFF status codes | Unchanged: still 200 for each API response. Ticket 10 changes this. |

## Checks

- The web typecheck and a full `next build` pass.
- I sent read-only requests to your running dev server on port 3000: the five BFF routes return data and the five pages return 200.
- `yarn verify`: jscpd passes with zero clones, knip is back to its baseline, and ESLint is down to 19 errors. The remaining ESLint errors are in customers and treatments code, which this ticket leaves alone.

## Two things to know

- **The customers and treatments BFF handlers changed too.** They used the same hardcoded URL and public key, so they had to move to the client. Their pages are untouched.
- **The BFF does not parse input with the contract schemas yet.** A BFF that rejects a body must return 400, and this ticket keeps the BFF at "always 200". I left a comment on ticket 10 to add the parse there, with the status forwarding.

## Planned commits

| # | Message | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `refactor: call the API through one server-only client` | `apps/web/lib/api.ts`, the four existing BFF `route.ts` files, `apps/web/.env.example` |
| 2 | `refactor: get the Overview summary through the BFF` | `apps/web/app/api/appointments/summary/route.ts`, `apps/web/app/page.tsx` |
| 3 | `refactor: take the appointment page types from the contract` | `apps/web/app/appointments/page.tsx`, `apps/web/app/appointments/[id]/confirmation/page.tsx` |

I will report the review findings and give you the final commit commands when both reviewers finish.

content.text:
Ticket 03, "Appointments web through the contract", is reviewed and ready for you to commit. The web typecheck is clean, and the BFF routes still answer on your running dev server after the fixes.

## Review

### Spec

All six acceptance criteria hold, with no blocking finding. The reviewer compared the old and the new BFF on your running servers: the same requests go to the API, and an API 404 still comes back as 200 with the same body. `POST` and `PATCH` were checked by reading only, because I told the reviewer not to write to your data.

It found one real gap, which I fixed: `lib/api.ts` was server-only by convention. It now imports the `server-only` package, so a client component that imports it fails the build. This adds one small dependency to the web app.

### Standards

No hard violation. I applied four fixes: a comment on the `Customer` and `Treatment` types, the rename to `ProxyOptions`, a JSDoc that states the status is always 200, and the orphaned comment in the confirmation page.

**Summary:** Standards has 4 judgement calls, the worst being types that assert a contract no schema defines. Spec has 3 findings, the worst being the missing `server-only` guard, now fixed.

## One risk to know

A developer with an old `.env.local` that still sets `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` gets no key sent, with no message. Against an API that requires a key, the pages then crash. No such file exists in this repo, and the new `.env.example` names the new variables. I recommend one line in `NOTES.md` when you write up the environment change.

## Commands

```bash
# 1. The API client and the BFF handlers
git add apps/web/lib/api.ts apps/web/app/api/appointments/route.ts "apps/web/app/api/appointments/[id]/route.ts" apps/web/app/api/customers/route.ts apps/web/app/api/treatments/route.ts apps/web/.env.example apps/web/package.json yarn.lock
git commit -m "refactor: call the API through one server-only client" -m "The BFF reads API_URL and API_KEY, which are server-only. NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY is gone, so the key no longer ships to the browser."

# 2. The Overview summary
git add apps/web/app/api/appointments/summary/route.ts apps/web/app/page.tsx
git commit -m "refactor: get the Overview summary through the BFF"

# 3. Page types
git add apps/web/app/appointments/page.tsx "apps/web/app/appointments/[id]/confirmation/page.tsx"
git commit -m "refactor: take the appointment page types from the contract"

# 4. Ticket updates
git add .scratch
git commit -m "docs: record the work on tickets 01 to 03"
```

Run `yarn workspace @venue/web typecheck` after each of the first three. The API suite does not cover the web app, so it tells you nothing here.

Phase 1 is complete with this ticket. The next tickets are the fixes, 04 to 11, and they have no order among them. I recommend 04, "Overlap rules", first.

content.text:
Yes, tag it. A tag costs nothing, does not rewrite history, and gives the reviewers a fixed point for "the refactor ends here, with behaviour unchanged".

## Name it for what it marks

The brief's Phase 1 has two parts: the refactor, and "fix what you'd flag if this came to you as a pull request". Tickets 04 to 11 are that second part. So this point is the end of the behaviour-preserving refactor, not the end of Phase 1. I recommend the name `phase-1-refactor`.

## Command

Make the three ticket 03 commits first. Then:

```bash
git tag -a phase-1-refactor -m "Appointments refactor complete. The characterization suite is green and no valid response changed."
```

## Two things to do with it

- **Push it explicitly.** `git push` does not send tags. If you submit a private repo link, run `git push origin phase-1-refactor`. A zip with `.git` includes it.
- **Mention it in `NOTES.md`.** One line is enough: the reviewers can then run `git diff 5ffee74 phase-1-refactor` to see the whole refactor, and check out the tag to run their suite against it.

If you like this, the same works later for the other boundaries: after the fixes (`phase-1-fixes`), after the three features (`phase-2`) and after the release work (`phase-3`).

content.text:
Ticket 04, "Overlap rules", is implemented and the full suite is green at 79 tests. The two reviews are running and nothing is committed yet, so wait for my next message before you commit.

## What is done

| Fix | Change | Test that fails before it |
|---|---|---|
| Back-to-back is allowed | The overlap check uses `<` and `>`, not `<=` and `>=`. | The changed characterization test, and a new test for an appointment that ends as another starts |
| Cancelled appointments do not count | The check skips `cancelled` and the legacy `canceled`. | Two new tests, one per spelling |
| A moved appointment gets the check | `PATCH` with `startsAt` runs the overlap check and ignores the appointment itself. | A new test that expects 409 |

Two more tests guard the edges of the third fix: an appointment can move within its own old slot, and a cancelled appointment can move anywhere.

## The characterization test

I changed one test in `apps/api/test/characterization/appointments.test.ts`, which is the case the brief requires. "rejects an appointment that starts as another one ends" (409) is now "accepts an appointment that starts as another one ends" (201). It goes in its own commit, before the fix, so the history shows it red and then green.

## One decision I made

A `PATCH` skips the overlap check when the appointment is cancelled, or becomes cancelled in the same request. A cancelled appointment does not count, so it cannot double-book anyone.

## How the commits will work

The three fixes all edit the same service file, so you cannot split them with `git add` at the end. I saved a copy of the changed files after each step in my scratch directory, and ran the suite at each one. When the reviews are in, I will give you one short script that copies each step into place and commits it, four commits in order.

content.text:
Yes, for this one test. The brief names this exact case and says how to handle it:

> If a test encodes a bug, don't edit it quietly. Say so in NOTES.md and change it in its own commit.

## Why this test qualifies

The test expected 409 for an appointment that starts at 10:30 when another ends at 10:30. The README says the opposite: "Back-to-back is fine: one can end at 10:30 and the next start at 10:30." The README also says that when the code and a rule disagree, the rule is right. So the test recorded a bug.

## Why it cannot stay as it was

The fix and the old test cannot both hold. After the fix, the API returns 201 for that request, and the old test fails.

| Option | Result |
|---|---|
| Change the test to expect 201 (what I did) | The rule is fixed, and the suite records the correct behaviour. |
| Delete the test | The rule is fixed, but nothing guards it in their suite. |
| Leave the test and the bug | The suite stays untouched, but the API breaks a stated business rule. |

## What makes it acceptable

Three things, and all are in place or queued:

- **Its own commit.** The test change is a separate commit, with nothing else in it.
- **A line in `NOTES.md`.** It names the test, the old and new expectation, and the rule. I add it before you commit.
- **Nothing else in that folder changes.** The diff is one test: its title, one comment, and `409` to `201`.

This is also the exception in the note I saved after your earlier instruction: no new files in that folder, and a change only where the brief requires one.

## One consequence to know

The test change goes in before the fix, so at that one commit the suite has one red test. I chose that order on purpose: the history then shows the test failing before the fix and passing after it, which is what the brief asks of a bug fix. The other order also leaves one red commit, so a red commit cannot be avoided without putting the test change and the fix together.

Ticket 04, "Overlap rules", is reviewed and ready to commit. The full suite passes at each of the three fix steps: 74, 76 and 79 tests.

## Review

### Spec

The three fixes are correct. The reviewer probed every arrangement of two appointments (touching at either end, contained, containing, identical), the 404, 400 and 409 order on `PATCH`, and that a rejected `PATCH` changes nothing. It also confirmed the arithmetic in the legacy-spelling test.

It found one hole that this ticket makes easier to reach: a `PATCH` that changes only the status from `cancelled` to `confirmed` gets no overlap check. A booking can now sit on the time of a cancelled appointment, so that `PATCH` double-books the customer. Ticket 05 closes it, because a cancelled appointment then cannot get another status. I left a comment on ticket 05 with the exact test to add. Until ticket 05 is in, the hole is open.

### Standards

I fixed three findings: the type `Slot` is now `OverlapCheck` (the glossary says to avoid "slot"), the new success tests assert the body as well as the status, and `NOTES.md` has a new section for changed characterization tests. I left the missing transaction, which ticket 07 owns.

**Summary:** Standards has 4 findings, the worst being a glossary term to avoid. Spec has 3 findings, the worst being the status-only revival of a cancelled appointment.

## Commit it

The three fixes edit the same file, so I wrote a script that replays the saved steps as four commits:

```bash
bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aesbetancourt-Dev-personal-interviews-treatwell-ai-engineer-take-home/9fbffbed-3a36-4b27-83e4-27fabc3b1389/scratchpad/ticket-04/commit.sh
```

It makes these commits, in order:

| # | Message | Suite at this commit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `test: expect 201 for a back-to-back appointment` | 1 red test, on purpose |
| 2 | `fix: allow back-to-back appointments` | 74 pass |
| 3 | `fix: do not count cancelled appointments in the overlap check` | 76 pass |
| 4 | `fix: check for an overlap when an appointment moves` | 79 pass |

The script only copies three files and runs `git add` and `git commit` on them. It stops at the start if you have anything staged. Read it first if you want; it is 45 lines. The files it ends on are identical to your working tree now, so nothing is lost if you prefer to commit by hand.

Afterwards, commit the ticket files as before:

```bash
git add .scratch
git commit -m "docs: record the work on ticket 04"
```

The next ticket is 05, "Status rules", and it closes the hole above, so I recommend it next.

Ticket 05, "Status rules", is implemented and the full suite is green at 87 tests. The two reviews are running and nothing is committed, so wait for my next message before you commit.

## What is done

| Fix | Change | Test that fails before it |
|---|---|---|
| Cancelling is final | A `PATCH` that gives a cancelled appointment another status returns 409. This covers both stored spellings. | Two new tests, one per spelling |
| Legacy status spelling | Each read returns `cancelled` for a stored `canceled`. The summary counts both under `cancelled`. The filter `status=cancelled` matches both. | The changed legacy test, and three new tests for the list, the filter and the summary |

Three more tests guard what must stay allowed: `cancelled` on an appointment that is cancelled already, new notes on a cancelled appointment, and every other status change.

## Three things to know

- **The double-booking hole from ticket 04 is closed.** The first new test is that exact case: a cancelled appointment that sits on an occupied time cannot be confirmed.
- **The contract is stricter.** The response status is now one of the four statuses, with no `canceled`. The contract test that parses all seeded appointments passes, and the web typecheck is clean.
- **I changed one existing test of mine.** The legacy appointment test in `appointments-edges.test.ts` expected the stored `canceled`, and now expects `cancelled`. It goes in its own commit before the fix, as with the back-to-back test. It is outside the characterization folder.

## One decision I made

The filter `status=cancelled` matches both spellings now, not in ticket 14. Without it, the list would show three appointments as cancelled while the filter found one.

## How the commits will work

As with ticket 04, I saved the files after each step. When the reviews are in, I will give you one script that makes three commits: the first fix, the changed test, and the second fix.

Ticket 05, "Status rules", is reviewed and ready to commit. I replayed the three saved steps in the working tree and ran the suite at each one: 84 pass, then one red test on purpose, then 87 pass.

## Review

### Spec

Both fixes work. The reviewer probed a temporary API and found no request that brings a cancelled appointment back, for both spellings and for `PATCH` bodies with several fields. No response of the API holds `canceled` any more, and the summary total and revenue are unchanged.

It found one real defect, which I fixed: `PATCH {status: 'cancelled'}` on a legacy appointment rewrote the stored `canceled` to `cancelled`, so the request did change something. The service now leaves the status of a cancelled appointment unwritten. I added a test for that request on a legacy appointment.

### Standards

I fixed three findings: the JSDoc of `updateAppointment` is one line again, `wasCancelled` is now `isAlreadyCancelled`, and the list test asserts the status code.

**Summary:** Standards has 3 hard findings, the worst being a boolean name against the naming rule. Spec has 4 findings, the worst being the rewritten stored status.

## Two things that stay open

- **`status=canceled` is still accepted by the list filter.** It returns only the legacy appointments, shown as `cancelled`. Ticket 14 rejects it with 400, and I left a comment there.
- **The web status filter still sends `canceled`.** The page then shows two of the three cancelled appointments. Ticket 10 fixes it.

One visible side effect on the page is correct: the Cancel button no longer shows on legacy cancelled appointments, because they now have the status `cancelled`.

bash /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aesbetancourt-Dev-personal-interviews-treatwell-ai-engineer-take-home/9fbffbed-3a36-4b27-83e4-27fabc3b1389/scratchpad/ticket-05/commit.sh

content.text:
Ticket 06, "Start times in UTC", is implemented and the full suite is green at 110 tests. The two reviews are running and nothing is committed, so wait for my next message before you commit.

## What is done

| Step | Change | Test |
|---|---|---|
| Generated column | `starts_at_utc` on `appointments`, with an index. Migration `0002_starts_at_utc.sql` is one `ALTER TABLE … ADD` and one `CREATE INDEX`, with no table rebuild. | 13 direct tests on a temporary database: winter, summer, both clock changes in 2026 and 2027, and a year in which 1 April is a Sunday |
| Legacy start times | Responses return `startsAt` in UTC for legacy appointments, with a correct `endsAt`. The overlap check and the list order use the UTC time. | The changed legacy test, plus three new tests that fail before the fix |
| Strict input | A new `startsAt` needs `Z` or an offset and is stored as UTC. A date-only value, a time with no zone and the legacy format return 400. | Five tests that fail before the fix, and two guards |

I checked each expected value in the direct test against the time zone database with `Intl` before I wrote it.

## Three things to know

- **The reminder job is not changed.** It still reads the stored start time, so the reminder window of a legacy appointment is off by the venue offset. The job has no test yet, and ticket 08 builds one. I moved this criterion to ticket 08 and left a comment there.
- **The contract is stricter again.** `startsAt` and `endsAt` in a response must now be ISO 8601 in UTC. The contract test that parses all seeded appointments passes.
- **One test depends on the old date filter.** "Stores a time with an offset in UTC" reads the stored value through `?date=`. Ticket 14 replaces that filter, so that test changes then.

## One edge I accepted

On the two clock-change days, one hour of local time is special. The expression treats the hour that does not exist in spring (02:00 to 02:59) and the hour that occurs twice in autumn as summer time. The spec reviewer is sweeping several years against the time zone database to confirm that these are the only differences.

## How the commits will work

Four commits from saved steps, as before: the column with its test, the changed test expectation, the legacy fix, and the strict-input fix. I will give you the script when the reviews are in.

content.text:
That sentence joined two separate facts, and the colon made it read as one rule. `CLAUDE.md` does not say anything about two statements.

## Fact 1: what `CLAUDE.md` requires

The "Database and migrations" section has this rule:

> Change `schema.ts`, then run `yarn db:generate`. Read the generated SQL before you commit it.

The reason is that drizzle-kit writes the migration for you, and it can write something you did not intend, such as a full table rebuild. You must look at the file before it goes into a commit.

## Fact 2: what the file holds

The file `apps/api/drizzle/0002_starts_at_utc.sql` is short, so the reading takes a minute. It has two SQL statements:

```sql
ALTER TABLE `appointments` ADD `starts_at_utc` text GENERATED ALWAYS AS (CASE WHEN … END) VIRTUAL;
CREATE INDEX `appointments_starts_at_utc_idx` ON `appointments` (`starts_at_utc`);
```

| Statement | What it does | What to check |
|---|---|---|
| `ALTER TABLE … ADD … VIRTUAL` | Adds the generated column. A virtual column stores nothing; SQLite computes it on read. | It is an `ADD`, with no `CREATE TABLE __new_appointments`, no copy and no `DROP TABLE`. Existing rows are untouched. |
| `CREATE INDEX` | Adds an index on the column, so the list can sort by it without a full scan. | It names only `starts_at_utc`. |

The long `CASE WHEN … END` part is the conversion from venue time to UTC. It is the same expression as in `apps/api/src/db/schema.ts`, where the comment explains it.

## What I meant

Read the file before you run the commit script, because the rule asks for it, and it is quick because the file has only those two statements. I had already read it, and the spec reviewer ran it against a table with existing rows.

Under sustained contention, can a request now wait up to 5 s and then fail with 500, and is that acceptable/documented?
4. PATCH: is the same race closed for moving an appointment (two replicas moving two appointments of one customer onto the same time, or one POST and one PATCH)? Is there a test for it? If not, say so as a gap and, if practical, probe it in the scratch copy.
5. Does any previously passing behaviour change (status codes, bodies, the 404/400/409 order on PATCH)? `yarn test` must stay green; report the count.
6. The test itself: could it pass for a wrong reason, is it flaky by design (timing, 25 rounds × 8 requests, the 20 s test timeout in apps/api/vitest.config.ts), does it clean up its processes and temp directory when an assertion fails, and does the new helper differ from the characterization helper in a way that matters?
Where you only reasoned from the code and did not run something, say so explicitly.

Ticket 07, "No double-booking across replicas", is implemented and the full suite is green at 113 tests. The two reviews are running and nothing is committed, so wait for my next message before you commit.

## What is done

| Item | Change |
|---|---|
| Transaction | The overlap check and the insert run in one synchronous immediate transaction. A `PATCH` runs its checks and its update the same way. |
| Database connection | It sets WAL mode and a busy timeout of 5 seconds. |
| Test helper | `apps/api/test/helpers/replicas.ts` starts several API processes on one seeded database. |
| Test | `apps/api/test/double-booking.test.ts` sends the same appointment to two replicas at once, 25 rounds with 8 requests each, and expects one 201 and seven 409 in each round. |

## The test fails before the fix

I ran the test three times on the code before the fix, and it failed all three times within the first three rounds, with two 201 responses for the same appointment. That is a real double-booking between two processes, which no one-process test can show. After the fix it passed three times in a row.

## Two things to know

- **The helper is a new file, outside the characterization folder.** The ticket said to extend the existing helper so it can start a second server. Your rule is to leave that folder alone, so I wrote a separate helper. It repeats about 30 lines of the original (find a free port, wait until the API answers).
- **The repository now exports `inWriteTransaction`.** The service passes it a function, and only the repository touches Drizzle. The queries inside use the module's one connection, so they are part of the transaction. I asked the spec reviewer to confirm this against the Drizzle source and with an experiment.

## Planned commits

The files of the two commits do not overlap, so no script is needed this time:

| # | Message | Files |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `chore: set WAL mode and a busy timeout on the database` | `apps/api/src/db/index.ts` |
| 2 | `fix: book and move an appointment in one transaction` | the repository, the service, `apps/api/test/helpers/replicas.ts`, `apps/api/test/double-booking.test.ts` |

I will confirm the commands when the reviews are in.

content.text:
Ticket 07, "No double-booking across replicas", is reviewed and ready to commit. The full suite passes at 114 tests, and the transaction is restored and green after my last check.

## Review

### Spec

Six of the seven criteria are met and proven by experiment; the seventh is the commit, which is yours. The reviewer ran three variants of the code, five runs each:

| Variant | Result |
|---|---|
| The fix as written | 0 of 5 runs fail. 25 accepted and 175 rejected, no 500. |
| No transaction | 5 of 5 fail, with 35 to 46 accepted appointments where 25 are correct. |
| A deferred transaction in place of the immediate one | 5 of 5 fail, with 14 to 21 responses of 500 per run. |

So both the transaction and the word `immediate` are necessary, and the test catches the removal of either. The reviewer also confirmed in the Drizzle source that queries on the module's connection run inside the transaction.

It found one gap, which I closed: moving an appointment had the same race and no test. I added a second test that moves two appointments of one customer to the same time through two replicas, and expects one 200 and one 409. I then removed the transaction temporarily and ran both tests twice: both failed each time.

### Standards

I applied five fixes: the test asserts the body of the accepted response, the busy timeout is set before WAL mode, the customer and treatment lookups now run inside the transaction, `inWriteTransaction` passes the function straight to Drizzle, and `applyUpdate` has a JSDoc. The helper also stops the replicas it started if a later one fails to start.

My doubt about one claim was right: the previous API version does wait for the lock during a rollout, because `better-sqlite3` sets a 5 second timeout by default. The `busy_timeout` line therefore changes nothing; it states the value the transaction depends on, and the comment says so.

**Summary:** Standards has 2 rule findings, the worst being a success response with no body assertion. Spec has 2 findings, the worst being the untested race on `PATCH`.

## Limits to know

`NOTES.md` now records these under "before this goes live":

- The transaction takes the write lock of the whole database, so every booking and every `PATCH` waits its turn.
- A replica that waits for the lock blocks its event loop for up to 5 seconds, then returns 500.
- WAL mode needs all replicas on one host.

All three come from SQLite. They belong in `docs/migrations.md` under the Postgres question, in ticket 22.

## Commit it

The two commits have no file in common:

```bash
git add apps/api/src/db/index.ts
git commit -m "chore: set a busy timeout and WAL mode on the database" -m "All API replicas share the database. The busy timeout is the default of better-sqlite3, stated because the booking transaction depends on it. WAL lets a replica read while another one writes."

git add apps/api/src/modules/appointments/appointments.repository.ts apps/api/src/modules/appointments/appointments.service.ts apps/api/test/helpers/replicas.ts apps/api/test/double-booking.test.ts
git commit -m "fix: book and move an appointment in one transaction" -m "Two replicas could both pass the overlap check and both write. The checks and the write now run in one immediate transaction. Two tests start two API processes on one database and fail without it."

git add .scratch
git commit -m "docs: record the work on ticket 07"
```

## One line for your `CLAUDE.md`

The Testing section says to use `startServer`. Add this line after it, so the rules file matches the code:

> Use `startReplicas` from `apps/api/test/helpers/replicas.ts` when a test needs several API processes on one database.

The next ticket is 08, "Exactly one reminder". It also picks up the reminder window for legacy appointments from ticket 06.

Ticket 07 rests on a business rule in the README, a planted defect in the starting code, and two decisions you approved in the grilling session. The brief does not name this fix; it falls under its open instruction to fix what you would flag in a pull request.

## The chain

| Source | What it says |
|---|---|
| README, business rules | "A customer can't be double-booked, so two of their appointments must never overlap." |
| README, production | "The API and the web app each run as three replicas… All the API replicas share one database." |
| Starting code, `routes.ts` | An in-memory set, `bookingInProgress`, with a comment that it stops two requests from both passing the overlap check. A set in one process cannot see the other two replicas, so the rule did not hold in production. |
| Brief, Phase 1 | "Beyond that, fix what you'd flag if this came to you as a pull request, and tell us what you found." |
| README, tests section | "If you find behaviour that breaks one of the business rules, fix it… Make the fix its own commit, with a test that would have caught the bug." |
| `docs/assessment.md` | Lists it under business-rule violations: "The in-memory `bookingInProgress` lock fails across three replicas." |
| Grilling, Q21 | You approved one test with two API processes on one database. |
| Grilling, Q22 | You approved the busy timeout and WAL mode. |
| `docs/plan.md`, Step 1b, fix 9 | "Booking race… one synchronous immediate transaction around the check and the insert." |

## Proof that the defect is real

It is not a theory. The new test starts two API processes on one database and sends them the same appointment. Before the fix, both accepted it in every run, so the customer was double-booked.

## What goes beyond what you approved

Two things came from the reviews, not from your answers:

- **The transaction also covers `PATCH`.** The plan names only the check and the insert. Moving an appointment had the same race, and the reviewer showed it failing, so I covered it and added a test.
- **The customer and treatment lookups moved inside the transaction.** This is for consistency between create and update. It changes no response.

## Is it required

No. The brief's hard requirements for Phase 1 are the layers, the schemas, the typed errors and the shared contract. This ticket is one of the fixes you chose to add when you told me to ignore the time budget.

If you think it goes too far, the alternative is to drop the two commits and describe the race in `NOTES.md` as a known defect with its fix. I recommend keeping it: the reviewers ask "whether your tests would catch a real regression", and this is the one test in the repo that exercises the production model they describe.

# **Appointment Booking Platform** 

You’ll work on the backoffice of a beauty and wellness venue, a small app that is messy on purpose. You’ll refactor one module, build three features on top of it, then make the schema changes safe to ship. 


### **Ground rules.** 

- Don’t squash or rewrite your commit history. 

Read the README first. It covers setup, the business rules (treat them as the specification), the API contract and how the app runs in production. 

## **The characterization tests** 

`apps/api/test/characterization` describes how the API behaves today. 

- Keep it green through Phase 1. A refactor must not change what the endpoints return. 

- If a test encodes a bug, don’t edit it quietly. Say so in NOTES.md and change it in its own commit. 

- If you find a bug the suite doesn’t cover, fix it in its own commit, with a test. 

## **Phase 0: rules file (about 20 minutes)** 

Before writing code, add a short `CLAUDE.md` (or your tool’s equivalent) with the conventions you’ll follow: layering, errors, validation, naming, testing, what not to do. We compare it with your code. 

## **Phase 1: refactor appointments (about 90 minutes)** 

Refactor the appointments module only, in the API and the web pages that use it. Leave customers and treatments alone, apart from what appointments needs. This is the template for Phase 2. 

At a minimum: 

- Routes, services and repositories, with only the repository touching Drizzle. ● Schemas for input and output (zod, for example), with types inferred from them. 

- Typed errors and one consistent error response. 

- One contract shared by the API and the BFF. Where it lives is up to you. 

Beyond that, fix what you’d flag if this came to you as a pull request, and tell us what you found. 

## **Phase 2: three features (about 90 minutes)** 

Each feature should look like your Phase 1 module. We run our own tests against these contracts, so follow the shapes exactly. The UI is up to you. 

### **1. Staff members.** 

- A `staff` table: `id` , `name` , `email` (unique, case-insensitive), `active` (default true) and `createdAt` . Use a generated Drizzle migration, not `drizzle-kit push` . 

- Responses are `{ id, name, email, active, createdAt }` , with `createdAt` in ISO 8601. 

- Endpoints: 

   - `GET /staff` : an array ordered by name; 

   - `GET /staff/:id` ; 

   - `POST /staff` with `name` and `email` : returns 201; 

   - `PATCH /staff/:id` with any of `name` , `email` , `active` : returns 200. 

- Errors: 
   - 409 for a duplicate email; 
   - 404 for an unknown id; 
   - 400 for invalid input (a blank name, a malformed email, a non-boolean `active` , an empty PATCH). 

- BFF routes, a list page and a create form. 

### **2. Pagination, filtering and sorting on** **`GET /appointments` .** 

- Parameters: 

   - `page` : from 1, default 1; 
   - `pageSize` : 1 to 100, default 20; 
   - `status` : `pending` , `confirmed` , `completed` or `cancelled` ; 
   - `from` and `to` : `YYYY-MM-DD` , both inclusive, as dates in Europe/Berlin; 
   - `sortBy` : `startsAt` (default), `createdAt` or `price` ; 
   - `sortDir` : `asc` (default) or `desc` . 

- These replace the `date` filter. Any other value returns 400. 

- The response is `{ items, page, pageSize, total }` . Items keep today’s shape, `total` counts every match, and a page past the end returns empty `items` . 

- Update the characterization tests this breaks, and say so in NOTES.md. 

- In the UI, keep all of these in the URL so a page can be reloaded and shared. 

### **3. Soft delete with an audit trail.** 

- `DELETE /appointments/:id` returns 204. A deleted appointment disappears from reads, lists, the summary and the double-booking check. Deleting an unknown or already-deleted appointment returns 404. 

- Every create, update and delete writes an audit entry, in the same transaction as the change. 

- `GET /appointments/:id/audit` returns `{ action, appointmentId, at, changes }` , oldest first: 

   - `action` is `create` , `update` or `delete` ; 
   - `at` is ISO 8601; 
   - for an update, `changes` maps each changed field to `{ from, to }` . What it holds for create and delete is up to you. 

- Deleted appointments keep their audit trail. An appointment that never existed returns 404. 

- A delete button on the appointment page, with a confirmation step. 

If time runs out, stop cleanly. Features 1 and 2 done well beat three half-done. 

## **Phase 3: ship it safely (about 45** 

## **minutes)** 

Picture several API instances behind a load balancer, zero-downtime deploys and a database full of customer data. It’s SQLite here, but treat it like a real production database. 

- Make migrations a deliberate release step: 

   - `yarn db:migrate` applies pending migrations and exits; 

   - starting the API with `NODE_ENV=production` must not create or alter tables; 

   - `yarn dev` must still work from a fresh clone. 

- Add a migration that fixes the legacy `canceled` spelling. It must be safe on existing data and safe to run twice. 

- Add `yarn db:check` in `apps/api` , failing when `schema.ts` has changes no migration covers, and add it to `yarn verify` . 

- Add a small, production-ready Dockerfile for each app. No CI, Kubernetes manifests or cloud setup. 

- Write `docs/migrations.md` , half a page at most, answering: 

   - who runs migrations, when, from which image and with what permissions; 

   - whether the previous API version still works against each migration, and why that matters; 

   - how you’d roll back a bad release; 

   - what you’d do differently on Postgres with several instances. 

Our tests run `db:migrate` , `db:seed` and `start` , in that order, so keep those script names. 

## **What to send** 

A private repo link, or a zip that includes `.git` , containing: 

1. Your code, with your real commit history in small commits. 

2. Your rules file, as it stood at the end. 

3. `NOTES.md` , one page at most, answering: 

   - What did you decide, and why? 

   - What did you skip, and why? 

   - Where did the AI get something wrong, and how did you catch it? 

   - What would you do next with another day? 

   - What would you want in place before this goes live? 

4. `docs/migrations.md` . 

5. Optional: your AI session transcripts (Claude Code keeps them in `~/.claude/projects` ) or a screen recording of up to 5 minutes. 

Run `yarn verify` before you submit, and tell us about anything it still reports. 

## **How we review** 

Two engineers review your submission separately, reading NOTES.md first, then the commits, then the code. Our tests and `yarn verify` are signals, not pass or fail. We look most at: 

- whether you protected existing behaviour; 

- whether the features match your refactor; 

- whether the diffs are no bigger than each change needed; 

- whether your tests would catch a real regression; 

- how honest your notes are. 

You’ll walk us through your work and make a small change live with your tools. Expect questions about anything in the repo, whoever wrote it.

Ticket 07 agrees with the brief; nothing in it conflicts with these instructions. It is implemented and green (114 tests), and not committed yet.

## Ticket 07 against the brief

| Brief line | How ticket 07 meets it |
|---|---|
| "If you find a bug the suite doesn't cover, fix it in its own commit, with a test." | The double-booking race is not in the characterization suite. The fix is one `fix` commit with `double-booking.test.ts`, which fails without the transaction. |
| "fix what you'd flag if this came to you as a pull request, and tell us what you found" | The in-memory `bookingInProgress` lock cannot work across replicas. `NOTES.md` records it. |
| "Picture several API instances behind a load balancer… treat it like a real production database." | The test starts two API processes on one database. |
| "Every create, update and delete writes an audit entry, in the same transaction as the change." | Ticket 17 needs `inWriteTransaction`, so this is not extra work. |
| "whether your tests would catch a real regression" | Both tests fail in every run when the transaction is removed. |
| "Keep it green through Phase 1." | No characterization test changed. |

The brief also says "whether the diffs are no bigger than each change needed". The `chore` commit is the part a reviewer can question:

- `busy_timeout = 5000` is already the default of `better-sqlite3`. The line only states it.
- `journal_mode = WAL` is a real change, and it needs all replicas on one host. `NOTES.md` says so.

## What changed

| Commit | Change | Test that fails before it |
|---|---|---|
| `refactor: run the reminder job through the appointments repository` | The job no longer imports Drizzle. It takes the mailer and the clock as parameters. | None (it adds no test) |

| `fix: read a legacy start time as venue time in the reminder job` | The 24 hour window uses `toUtcStart`. | A legacy appointment at exactly 24 hours got no reminder; one that started a minute ago got one |
| `fix: state the start time in venue time in the reminder email` | New constant `VENUE_TIME_ZONE` in the contract. The email said the server time (UTC in production). | The email said 20:00 for a 22:00 appointment |

**Standards:** no hard violation. I left these judgement calls as they are: the 24 hour rule is in the job and not in a service, and the "confirmed without reminder" condition appears twice in the repository.

**Spec:** no blocking defect. I acted on three findings:

- **The ADR was wrong.** It said a reminder is lost only on a crash. A send that the provider rejects also loses it, because the job does not retry. The ADR and `NOTES.md` now say so.
- **The legacy tests were 30 minutes inside the window.** They now sit on the edge, as the ticket asks.
- **A behaviour change in the refactor commit.** An appointment with a missing customer row made the old job throw. Now the job skips it. `NOTES.md` records it.

- **The fourth commit (email in venue time).** The ticket does not ask for it. I added it because the email told the customer the wrong hour.
- **The claim also requires the status `confirmed`.** An appointment cancelled a moment before then gets no reminder. No test covers this, because a direct test cannot cancel between the read and the claim.

content.text:
Ticket 09 (**Confirmation page without notes**) is implemented and reviewed. The suite is green with 122 tests. It is not committed.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `packages/contract/src/appointments.ts` | New `publicAppointmentSchema`: id, start, end, status, price, customer name, treatment name and duration. New `appointmentIdParamSchema` (digits only). |
| `apps/web/app/api/appointments/[id]/confirmation/route.ts` | New BFF route. It returns the public schema or a fixed error (404 or 502). It never sends an API body as it is. |
| `apps/web/app/appointments/[id]/confirmation/page.tsx` | The page calls the new route. It shows a message when the request fails; before, it crashed. |
| `apps/web/lib/api.ts` | New `requestApi`, which returns the status and the body. `proxyToApi` uses it and behaves as before. |
| `apps/api/test/contract.test.ts` | One test: the public schema of the real API response holds exactly the eight fields. |

## Checked by hand on your dev server

| Request | Result |
|---|---|
| `/api/appointments/1/confirmation` | 200, no `notes`, email or phone |
| `/api/appointments/999/confirmation`, `/abc/`, `..%2Fcustomers` | 404 with the fixed error body |
| API `GET /appointments/1` | Unchanged |

## Review

Both reviews found no leak. I fixed these findings:

- The test did not assert the status code.
- A new string used the word "booking", which the glossary avoids.
- The route forwarded the raw API body on an error, and threw when the API body did not match the schema. Both paths now return a fixed error.

Three limits remain, and `NOTES.md` records them:

- **No automated test calls the BFF route.** The web app has no test runner. The test covers the schema only.
- **The staff route `/api/appointments/:id` still returns `notes`** to anyone who has the URL, because the web app has no authentication.
- **Appointment ids are sequential**, so anyone can read a confirmation by its id.

`yarn verify` still fails on ESLint and knip, in files this ticket did not touch.

Ticket 10 (**Appointments page fixes**) is implemented and reviewed. The suite is green with 132 tests. It is not committed.

## The four fixes

| Commit | Change |
|---|---|
| `fix: forward the API status code from the appointment BFF handlers` | List, create, read, update and summary forward the status code and the body of the API. When the API does not answer, they return 502 with the contract error body. `POST` and `PATCH` parse the body with the contract. An id must be digits only. |
| `fix: show the error in the create form and keep it open` | A rejected appointment shows its reason, and the form keeps its values. |
| `fix: send cancelled from the status filter` | One word. The filter now shows appointments 6, 11 and 12; before, only 11 and 12. |
| `fix: enter and show appointment times in venue time` | New `venueTimeToUtc` and `formatVenueTime` in `packages/contract/src/venue.ts`. The form, the list and the confirmation page use them. |

## How it was checked

- **Venue time:** `apps/api/test/venue-time.test.ts` has 10 cases, including both clock changes. A round trip of 350,640 half-hour instants from 2020 to 2040 differs only in the 40 cases of the hour that occurs twice in October, as the test documents.
- **BFF:** requests that the API rejects, through your dev server: 409 for an overlap, 400 for an invalid body, 404 for an unknown id and for `..%2Fcustomers` as an id.
- **Each step:** I replayed the four steps; typecheck and lint pass at each one.

## Review findings

I fixed these:

- `errorResponse` took four positional parameters; it now takes one options object.
- The confirmation route threw when the API did not answer; it now returns 502.
- The form showed nothing on a network failure, and kept an old error when it was closed and opened again.

These remain, and `NOTES.md` or ticket 14 records each one:

- **Fixes 1 to 3 have no test that fails before them.** The web app has no test runner. This departs from the commit rule in `CLAUDE.md`.
- **The list handler forwards the query string without a parse**, and the `date` filter still matches the stored text. Ticket 14 replaces both.
- **`PATCH` with an unknown id and an invalid body** returns 400 from the BFF and 404 from the API.
- **A rejected Confirm or Cancel click shows no message.** The ticket does not ask for it.
- **The hour that occurs twice in October** reads as winter time in the form and as summer time for a legacy appointment.

`yarn verify` still fails on ESLint and knip, in files this ticket did not touch.

## Commit

```bash
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aesbetancourt-Dev-personal-interviews-treatwell-ai-engineer-take-home/9fbffbed-3a36-4b27-83e4-27fabc3b1389/scratchpad/ticket-10/commit.sh
```

It makes the four `fix` commits and one `docs: close ticket 10` commit. Next is `/implement 11` (hardening).

message.content: It's getting really slow to solve the tickets why? The agents review are consuming too much time

content.text:
The reviews are one cause, but not the largest. The measured times for the last three tickets:

| Step | Time per ticket | Note |
|---|---|---|
| Two review agents (parallel) | 1 to 3 minutes | 43 s to 163 s wall-clock, about 110k tokens |
| Fixes after the review | 2 to 4 minutes | Each review returns 6 to 10 findings, most of them judgement calls |
| Snapshots and replay per commit | 2 to 3 minutes | Needed because I cannot commit, and the commits share files |
| `yarn test` and `yarn verify`, several runs | 1 to 2 minutes | The suite takes 16 s, and it starts real API processes |
| Checks by hand on the dev server | 1 to 2 minutes | The web app has no test runner |

So the review itself is short. The slow part is what it triggers: I act on the findings, then save the steps and replay them again.

## Options

| Option | Saves | Risk |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Review only the risky tickets** (recommended) | About half the time on the others | A small defect slips through on a simple ticket |
| B. One review agent in place of two | About 1 minute | Small |
| C. No review agents; I read my own diff | Most | I miss what a second reader finds, as with the wrong ADR claim in ticket 08 |
| D. You let me commit | 2 to 3 minutes per ticket | None for quality; you lose the manual step |

For A, I would keep the two-agent review for tickets 14 (paginated list), 16 and 17 (delete and audit), 18 to 20 (migrations and `db:check`), and skip it for 11, 12, 13, 15, 21, 22. Those are the tickets where the brief's external tests run or where a mistake touches data.

D is independent of the others and is the largest single saving: with commit permission, I commit after each step and need no snapshots, no replay and no script.

Tell me which option you want, and whether to combine it with D. Until then I keep the current flow.

content.text:
Ticket 14 (**Paginated appointment list**) is done, reviewed and committed. The suite is green with 215 tests.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `7ea5fdc test: expect the paginated list in the characterization tests` | The six `GET /appointments` tests, alone. Red until the next commit. |
| `a07f3a1 feat: paginate, filter and sort the appointment list` | Contract, repository, service, and 55 new tests |
| `a533059 feat: show the appointment list in pages` | The BFF parses the query. The page has From, To, Previous and Next. |
| `769901a fix: read the page and the total in one transaction, and reverse ties with the sort` | Two review findings |

The new tests cover each parameter, 29 cases of 400, a page past the end, `from` later than `to`, and venue midnight for new and legacy appointments.

## Review

Two agents, 43 and 91 seconds. No hard spec violation. The Spec agent probed the running API with odd inputs. I fixed these:

- **The total and the items came from two statements.** A write between them made them disagree. One read transaction now covers both.
- **`desc` was not the exact reverse of `asc` for equal prices.** The id tiebreak now follows the direction. A test of the form "desc equals reversed asc" passes now, and a test that only checks the prices passes either way.
- Two naming breaches of `CLAUDE.md`, and three missing status assertions.

One mistake of mine: commit `769901a` holds two fixes, and `CLAUDE.md` says one per commit. The history cannot be rewritten, so it stays.

## Risks with the external tests

These are decisions, not defects. `NOTES.md` states each one:

| Behaviour | Why |
|---|---|
| An unknown parameter returns 400 | Your grilling answer. The brief says "any other value", which is less clear for a parameter name. |
| `page=01` returns 200 | It is the number 1. |
| `from` later than `to` returns 200 with no items | Your grilling answer. |

## Open points

- **The list state is not in the URL yet**, and the page has no sort control. That is ticket 15.
- **A rolling update breaks the old web version** for a moment, because the response shape changes in one release. `NOTES.md` records it; `docs/migrations.md` in ticket 22 is the place to state it.
- **The legacy boundary test calls the service directly**, because the API cannot create a legacy appointment.

`yarn verify` still fails on ESLint and knip, in files this ticket did not touch. The ticket files and `NOTES.md` are not committed. Next is `/implement 15`.

Ticket 16 (**Delete an appointment**) is done, reviewed and committed. The suite is green with 238 tests.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `174428b test: add delete to the test server helper` | The one change in the characterization folder, alone |

## Review

Two agents, 32 and 79 seconds. The Standards review found no hard violation. The Spec review confirmed that all nine appointment queries leave a deleted appointment out, and that eight deletes at the same time give one 204 and seven 404. It found two real defects by probing the API:

| Finding | Fix |

| **A `DELETE` with a JSON content type and no body returned 400.** Fastify rejected it before the route ran. A test client that always sets that header would get 400 where the brief says 204. | The API ignores the content type on a `DELETE`. |
| A failed delete showed nothing on the page. | The page shows a message. |

`NOTES.md` records the first one as an AI mistake that the review caught.

## Open points

- **Rolling update:** a replica of the previous version still shows a deleted appointment, counts it in the overlap check and sends its reminder, until the rollout ends. You accepted this window in the grilling session; `NOTES.md` states it, and ticket 22 puts it in `docs/migrations.md`.
- **No audit entry yet.** That is ticket 17, which puts the delete and its entry in one transaction.

content.text:
Ticket 17 (**Audit trail**) is done, reviewed and committed. The suite is green with 257 tests. This closes Phase 2.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `c02bb8e feat: add the appointment audit table` | Generated migration `0005`: one new table and one index. Audit schemas in the contract. |
| `4217873 feat: record and read the audit trail of an appointment` | An entry for each create, update and delete, in the transaction of the change. `GET /appointments/:id/audit`. 18 tests. |
| `07c787a test: …` and `201d6b5 refactor: …` | Review findings |

## How it behaves

| Case | Result |
|---|---|
| Create | Each of the six fields, `from: null` |
| Update | Only the fields that changed |
| A `PATCH` that changes no value | 200, no entry, no write |
| Delete | Each field, `to: null`. The trail stays readable (200). |
| An id that never existed | 404 |
| A seeded appointment with no change | 200 with `[]` |
| A legacy appointment | The trail shows what the API shows: a UTC start time and `cancelled` |

One direct test proves the shared transaction: with the audit table removed, a create, an update and a delete each fail and leave no change.

## Review

Two agents, 40 and 90 seconds. The Spec agent probed a temporary API and found no shape or status defect. It confirmed the two inputs an external test most likely sends: `PATCH {status:'confirmed'}` on appointment 3 gives exactly `{"status":{"from":"pending","to":"confirmed"}}`, and notes on an appointment with null notes gives `{"notes":{"from":null,"to":"hello"}}`.

I fixed: missing status assertions, a missing test that the reminder mark writes no entry, a service name that did not match the glossary, and two timestamps in one delete.

Three decisions carry a small risk with the external tests. `NOTES.md` states each one:

- **A seeded appointment has no create entry.** A test that expects one for appointment 1 fails. Your grilling answer set this (200 with `[]`).
- **A `PATCH` that repeats the current value writes no entry.** Your grilling answer.
- **`applyUpdate` changed:** a `PATCH` with the same start time no longer runs the overlap check or rewrites a legacy start time. No response changed for the seed data.

`yarn verify` still fails on ESLint and knip, in files this ticket did not touch. The ticket files and `NOTES.md` are not committed.

## Tags

This is the point for the Phase 2 tag, and the Phase 1 tag is still missing:

```bash
git tag -a phase-1-fixes 72f0820 -m "Phase 1 complete: the appointments refactor and the fixes for the business rules, the web pages and the hardening."
git tag -a phase-2-features 201d6b5 -m "Phase 2 complete: staff members, the paginated appointment list, and soft delete with the audit trail."
```

Next is `/implement 18` (migrations as a release step).

content.text:
Ticket 18 (**Migrations as a release step**) is done, reviewed and committed as `7d60c7f`. The suite is green with 263 tests.

## What changed

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `apps/api/src/db/index.ts` | It only opens the connection. The migration on load is gone. |
| `apps/api/src/db/migrate-cli.ts` | The release step: it applies the pending migrations and exits. |
| `apps/api/src/index.ts` | The seed on start never runs when `NODE_ENV` is `production`. |
| `apps/api/package.json` | `dev` runs `db:migrate` first. `db:migrate`, `db:seed` and `start` keep their names. |
| `apps/api/test/migrations.test.ts` | Six tests that start real processes and read the database file. |

## The brief's three points

| Requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| `yarn db:migrate` applies pending migrations and exits | Test: exit code 0, all five tables exist. A second run leaves the schema and the migration count unchanged. |
| A start with `NODE_ENV=production` creates or alters no table | Test: a start on an empty database leaves zero tables. The same holds in development. |
| `yarn dev` works from a fresh clone | I ran the `dev` script on a new database path and a spare port: it migrated, started, seeded, and returned 14 appointments. |

Three of the six tests failed before the change, for the expected reasons.

## Review

UPDATE `appointments` SET `status` = 'cancelled' WHERE `status` = 'canceled';

| Condition | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Safe on existing data | The test brings a database to the schema before the fix, adds six appointments, and applies the migrations as `db:migrate` does. Only the two `canceled` rows change. A legacy start time, the price, and a note that holds the word "canceled" stay as they are. |

Ticket 20 (**`yarn db:check`**) is done, reviewed and committed.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `1fda339 feat: add yarn db:check` | `apps/api/src/db/check-cli.ts`, the `db:check` script in `apps/api` and at the root, a new step in `scripts/verify.mjs`, three tests |
| `5f2cd7c fix: say what to do when db:check meets a rename` | From the review |

## How it works

It copies the migrations folder, runs `drizzle-kit generate` against the copy, and fails when a new file appears. It passes only on the message "nothing to migrate", because `generate` exits with 0 for each result. It removes the copy in each case.

## Probe results from the review

The review agent changed `schema.ts` in ten ways, ran the check, and restored the file byte for byte:

| Schema change | Exit code |
|---|---|
| None | 0 |
| New nullable column, new table, new index, changed default, removed column | 1 each |
| Renamed column, renamed table | 1 |
| Comment only, type-only change | 0 |

Each run takes about one second, works from each directory, and leaves no file. Three runs at the same time do not disturb each other.

One finding, fixed: a rename failed with a `drizzle-kit` stack trace only, because `drizzle-kit` asks a question about a rename and has no terminal there. The check now names the cause and tells you to run `yarn db:generate`.

One small gap stays: `--schema=path` with an equals sign is ignored, and the real schema is checked. That option exists only for the tests.

## `yarn verify` now

It runs 7 checks. 5 pass, including `db:check`. ESLint and knip still fail, for the same reasons as before: lint errors in customers and treatments, and the unused `lodash`, `dayjs` and `utils/legacy.ts`.

The ticket files and `NOTES.md` are not committed. Next is `/implement 21` (Dockerfiles).

Ticket 21 (**Dockerfiles**) is done, reviewed and committed. The suite is green with 269 tests.

## Commits

| Commit | Content |
|---|---|
| `297b426 feat: add a production Dockerfile for each app` | `apps/api/Dockerfile`, `apps/web/Dockerfile`, `.dockerignore`, the standalone option in `next.config.ts`, `tsx` moved to `dependencies` |
| `89ab2fd fix: add a health check to the web image and keep more files out of the build` | From the review |

## What I ran

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Build the API image | 469 MB |
| Start it on an empty volume, before a migration | Starts, `/health` 200, data routes 500, no table made |
| `yarn db:migrate` in the image, two times | "migrations applied" both times |
| Start it with `API_KEY` | 200 with the key, 401 without, runs as user `node` |
| No seed in production | The list is empty until `db:seed` runs by hand |
| Health check and stop | `healthy`; stops at once with exit code 0 |
| Build the web image | 403 MB; the app part is 42 MB |
| Both images together | The web image reached the API: the BFF returned 14 appointments, and the staff and confirmation routes answered 200 |

The build check found one real defect, which I fixed before the commit: the web image did not hold `tsconfig.base.json`, so the Next build failed.

**Not verified:** commit `89ab2fd` adds the web health check and more `.dockerignore` lines after the last build. I did not build again. The health check command is the same one that works in the API image.

## What I did on your machine

- `colima` was stopped. I started it, and it is stopped again now.
- The web install needs about 1.8 GB, and your default VM has 2 GiB, so the web build was killed there. I did not change your default VM. I made a temporary profile `venue-build` with 4 GiB, and deleted it after.
- **Left in your default VM:** the image `venue-api`, the volume `venue-check`, and two stopped containers, `venue-api-check1` and `venue-api-check2`. My remove commands were denied. To clean up: `colima start && docker rm venue-api-check1 venue-api-check2 && docker volume rm venue-check && docker rmi venue-api`.

input.content:
# Migrations

**Who, when, where.** A release job runs `yarn db:migrate` one time for each release, before the first pod of the new version starts. It uses the API image of the new version: `docker run venue-api yarn db:migrate`. The job has a database role that can change the schema. The API pods have a role that can only read and write rows, and a start of the API never runs a migration. SQLite has no roles, so here the rule holds by code only. `yarn db:check` in `yarn verify` fails a build whose `schema.ts` has a change with no migration.

**The previous version must work on the new schema.** A rolling update runs the old and the new version together, and the migration runs first. So each migration only adds.

| Migration | Previous API version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `0002` column `starts_at_utc` | Works | Generated column. An old insert does not name it. |
| `0003` table `staff` | Works | New table. Old code does not read it. |
| `0004` column `deleted_at` | Works, with a gap | Nullable. An old pod still shows a deleted appointment, counts it as an overlap and sends its reminder. |
| `0005` table `appointment_audit` | Works, with a gap | A change through an old pod writes no audit entry. |
| `0006` status `canceled` | Works | The previous version reads both spellings. A second run changes no row. |

The two gaps last as long as the rollout. To close them, use two releases: the first adds the columns and reads them, the second starts to write them. The same rollout has one break that is not in the schema: `GET /appointments` changed its response shape, so release the web version that reads the new shape first.

**Rollback.** Roll back the image, not the schema. No migration is reversed: the old version ignores the new columns and tables. After a rollback, a deleted appointment is visible again, and changes get no audit entry. Take a database backup before the release job, for the case that a data migration is wrong.

**On Postgres with several instances.**

- Take an advisory lock in the release job, so only one job migrates.
- Set `lock_timeout`, and create an index with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`.
- Run a data fix such as `0006` in batches, not in one transaction.
- Replace the write lock on the whole database with an exclusion constraint on the customer and the time range. Then the database rejects a double-booking by itself.
- Replace the hand-written daylight-saving rule of `starts_at_utc` with `AT TIME ZONE 'Europe/Berlin'`.

# Migrations

**Who, when, where.** A release job runs `yarn db:migrate` one time for each release, from the API image of the new version, before the first pod of that version starts. `yarn start` never runs a migration. In production the job has a role that can change the schema, and the pods have a role that can only read and write rows. This repo cannot show that: SQLite has file access only. `yarn db:check` fails a build whose schema has no migration.

**The previous version must work on the new schema**, because a rolling update runs both versions together after the migration. `0000` and `0001` came with the starting code.

| Migration | Previous API version | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `0002` column `starts_at_utc` | Works | Generated column. An old insert does not name it. |
| `0003` `staff`, `0005` `appointment_audit` | Works | New tables. An old pod writes no audit entry. |
| `0004` column `deleted_at` | Works, with a gap | An old pod still shows a deleted appointment, changes it, counts it as an overlap and sends its reminder. |
| `0006` status `canceled` | Works | It rewrites data, not the schema. The previous version reads both spellings. |

The gaps last as long as the rollout. Two releases close them: the first adds the column and reads it, the second writes it. `GET /appointments` also has a new response shape, which the old web version cannot read.

**Rollback.** Roll back the image, not the schema. The old version ignores the new columns and tables, and it reads the rows that `0006` changed. A deleted appointment is visible again. Take a backup before the job: no migration has a reverse.

**On Postgres with several instances.** Take an advisory lock, so only one job migrates. Set `lock_timeout`. Create an index with `CONCURRENTLY`, outside the migration transaction. Run a data fix in batches. Store the end time, and replace the whole-database write lock with an exclusion constraint on customer and time range. Replace the hand-written daylight-saving rule with `AT TIME ZONE`.
