=================== 01-contract-package-and-typed-errors.md
# 01: Contract package and typed errors

**What to build:** One shared contract package holds the zod schemas for the current appointment responses, the appointment inputs and the error body. The API has typed errors and one error handler that makes one error body. No endpoint response changes.

**Blocked by:** None (can start immediately)

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] The contract package is a workspace package that the API and the web app can import as TypeScript source, with no build step
- [x] Each type comes from a schema with `z.infer`
- [x] The schemas describe what the API returns today, legacy values included
- [x] A thrown typed error becomes `{ error: { code, message, details? } }` with status 400, 404 or 409
- [x] Customers and treatments keep their current error bodies
- [x] The characterization suite is green after each commit
=================== 02-appointments-api-as-a-layered-module.md
# 02: Appointments API as a layered module

**What to build:** The appointment endpoints run through routes, a service, a repository and a mapper. Only the repository uses Drizzle. Each endpoint returns the same status code and body as before for valid input.

**Blocked by:** 01 Contract package and typed errors

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] Routes parse input with the contract schemas and map output
- [x] The service holds the overlap check, the price copy and the status check, and throws typed errors
- [x] The list uses one joined query, not one query per appointment
- [x] Query conditions use bound parameters; no `sql.raw` on user input remains
- [x] An unknown `status` value still returns 200 with an empty list
- [x] The response mapping exists in one place
- [x] Customers and treatments are unchanged
- [ ] Each commit is a `refactor` commit and the characterization suite is green after each one
- [x] `NOTES.md` states the one changed response: injection input returned 500 and now returns 200 with an empty list

## Comments

**From the review of ticket 01.** The input schemas in the contract are stricter than the current code. When the routes parse with them, these inputs change status. Keep the current status where the list says so, and record each remaining difference in `NOTES.md`.

- `PATCH` of an unknown id with an invalid body returns 404 today. Look up the appointment before the body parse to keep the 404.
- `GET /appointments?status=` (empty string) means "no filter" today. Keep that.
- `POST` with `customerId: -1` or `1.5` returns 404 today, and 400 with the schema.
- `POST` with `customerId: "1"` (a numeric string) is accepted today, and returns 400 with the schema.
- `POST` or `PATCH` with `notes: 5` is accepted today, and returns 400 with the schema.
- `GET /appointments?status=a&status=b` returns 200 with an empty list today, and 400 with the schema.
=================== 03-appointments-web-through-the-contract.md
# 03: Appointments web through the contract

**What to build:** The appointment pages and their BFF handlers use the shared contract. One server-only API client calls the API. The Overview page gets the summary through a BFF route. What the user sees does not change.

**Blocked by:** 01 Contract package and typed errors

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] Only the server-only API client calls the API; no page calls it directly
- [x] The API URL and the API key come from server-only environment variables; no `NEXT_PUBLIC` key remains
- [x] The appointment pages and the Overview take their types from the contract; no `any` remains in them
- [x] The BFF still returns 200 for each API response (ticket 10 changes this)
- [x] The customers and treatments pages are unchanged
- [x] `yarn dev` works and the four pages load
=================== 04-overlap-rules.md
# 04: Overlap rules

**What to build:** The overlap check follows the business rules: back-to-back is allowed, cancelled appointments do not count, and a moved appointment gets the check too.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] A booking that starts at the instant another appointment of the same customer ends returns 201
- [x] The characterization test that records the back-to-back bug changes in its own commit, and `NOTES.md` says so
- [x] A booking that overlaps only a cancelled appointment returns 201, for both status spellings
- [x] A `PATCH` of `startsAt` that causes an overlap returns 409; the appointment does not overlap itself
- [ ] Each of the three fixes is its own `fix` commit with a test that fails before the fix
=================== 05-status-rules.md
# 05: Status rules

**What to build:** Cancelling is final, and a legacy appointment shows the status `cancelled`.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] A `PATCH` that changes the status of a cancelled appointment returns 409
- [x] A `PATCH` that sets `cancelled` on a cancelled appointment returns 200 and changes nothing
- [x] Notes stay editable on a cancelled appointment
- [x] All other status changes stay allowed
- [x] Each read returns `cancelled` for a stored `canceled`
- [x] The summary counts both spellings under `cancelled`
- [ ] Each fix is its own `fix` commit with a test that fails before the fix

## Comments

**From the review of ticket 04.** A status-only `PATCH` from `cancelled` to `confirmed` gets no overlap check. After ticket 04, a booking can sit on the time of a cancelled appointment, so that `PATCH` double-books the customer. This ticket closes the hole, because a cancelled appointment cannot get another status. Add a test for exactly this case: book over a cancelled appointment, then try to confirm the cancelled one, and expect 409.

=================== 06-start-times-in-utc.md
# 06: Start times in UTC

**What to build:** Each appointment has one UTC start time, whatever its stored format. A legacy appointment returns `startsAt` as UTC ISO, and its `endsAt` is correct. A new `startsAt` must name its zone. See ADR 0002.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] A virtual generated column holds the UTC start time, added by a generated migration that adds a column and an index and rebuilds no table
- [x] The generated SQL is read before the commit
- [x] The conversion uses the EU daylight-saving rule for venue time (Europe/Berlin)
- [x] A direct test against a temporary database covers a winter time, a summer time and both clock-change days
- [x] `endsAt`, the overlap check and the list order use the UTC start time (the reminder window moved to ticket 08)
- [x] A legacy appointment returns `startsAt` as UTC ISO; `createdAt` stays epoch milliseconds
- [x] A new `startsAt` with `Z` or an offset is stored as UTC ISO; one with an offset returns the same instant in UTC
- [x] A `startsAt` with no zone, date-only input included, returns 400
- [ ] The legacy conversion and the strict input are separate `fix` commits, each with a test that fails before the fix
=================== 07-no-double-booking-across-replicas.md
# 07: No double-booking across replicas

**What to build:** Two API processes that share one database cannot both accept the same booking for one customer.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [x] The overlap check and the insert run in one synchronous immediate transaction
- [x] The price is inserted with the appointment in one statement
- [x] No in-memory lock remains
- [x] The database connection sets a busy timeout and WAL mode
- [x] A test helper starts several API processes on one database (a new helper outside the characterization folder)
- [x] A test starts two API processes on one database and sends the same booking to both at the same time: one 201, one 409, no 500
- [ ] The fix is its own `fix` commit; the test fails before it
=================== 08-exactly-one-reminder.md
# 08: Exactly one reminder

**What to build:** A customer gets one reminder for a confirmed appointment, with three replicas running the job. See ADR 0001.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** done, not committed

- [x] The job claims the appointment with one atomic update, and sends the email only when the claim changed one row
- [x] The job uses the appointments repository; it does not import Drizzle
- [x] A direct test runs the job twice at the same time with a fake mailer and expects one email
- [ ] The fix is its own `fix` commit; the test fails before it

## Comments

**From ticket 06.** The reminder job still reads the stored `startsAt` with `new Date`, so the 24 hour window of a legacy appointment is off by the venue offset. Ticket 06 left the job alone, because the job has no test yet. In this ticket, read the UTC start time (`toUtcStart` in the appointments mapper, through the repository), and add a direct test with a legacy appointment at the edge of the window.

=================== 09-confirmation-page-without-notes.md
# 09: Confirmation page without notes

**What to build:** The customer-facing confirmation page gets only what a customer can see. Notes, email and phone do not reach the browser.

**Blocked by:** 03 Appointments web through the contract

**Status:** done, not committed

- [x] The contract has a public appointment schema with no `notes`, no customer email and no customer phone
- [x] A separate BFF route serves the confirmation page and parses the API response with that schema
- [x] The response of that route contains none of the three fields
- [x] The API response is unchanged
- [x] `NOTES.md` states that sequential ids still let anyone read a booking
- [ ] The fix is its own `fix` commit
=================== 10-appointments-page-fixes.md
# 10: Appointments page fixes

**What to build:** The appointments page tells the truth: a rejected booking shows as rejected, the cancelled filter works, and times are in venue time.

**Blocked by:** 03 Appointments web through the contract

**Status:** done, not committed

- [x] Each appointment BFF handler forwards the status code of the API
- [x] The BFF returns the error body shape of the contract when the API fails
- [x] The create form shows the error and stays open when the API rejects the booking
- [x] The status filter sends `cancelled`
- [x] Times are entered and shown in venue time (Europe/Berlin), not browser time
- [ ] Each of the four fixes is its own `fix` commit

## Comments

**From ticket 03.** The BFF handlers do not parse input with the contract schemas yet. A BFF that rejects a body must return 400, and ticket 03 had to keep the BFF at "always 200". Add the input parse here, together with the status forwarding: parse the body of `POST` and `PATCH` with the contract schema, and return 400 with the contract error body when it fails.

=================== 11-hardening.md
# 11: Hardening

**What to build:** Three small changes that the production model needs.

**Blocked by:** 02 Appointments API as a layered module

**Status:** done, not committed

- [x] No log line prints an appointment request body
- [x] The API closes the server and exits when it gets `SIGTERM`
- [x] `GET /health` returns 200 without the API key
- [ ] Each change is its own commit
=================== 23-notes-check-and-cut.md
# 23: Notes: check and cut

**What to build:** `NOTES.md` is true and fits on one page.

**Blocked by:** 22 `docs/migrations.md`

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] Each line is checked against the commits; a line with no matching commit is corrected or removed
- [ ] It answers the five questions of the brief
- [ ] It names each characterization test that changed, with its commit
- [ ] It lists each AI mistake found during the work and how it was caught
- [ ] It is one page at most
=================== 24-final-verify.md
# 24: Final verify

**What to build:** The submission is checked as a whole.

**Blocked by:** All tickets 01 to 23

**Status:** ready-for-agent

- [ ] `yarn verify` is run, and `NOTES.md` gives the reason for each check that stays red
- [ ] A fresh clone starts with `yarn dev`, and each page loads
- [ ] `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, `start` in that order give a working API
- [ ] The commit history is small commits with no squash and no rewrite

# Issue tracker: Local Markdown

Issues and specs for this repo live as markdown files in `.scratch/`.

## Conventions

- One feature per directory: `.scratch/<feature-slug>/`
- The spec is `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`
- Implementation issues are one file per ticket at `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, never a single combined tickets file
- Triage state is recorded as a `Status:` line near the top of each issue file (see `triage-labels.md` for the role strings)
- Comments and conversation history append to the bottom of the file under a `## Comments` heading

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a new file under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/` (creating the directory if needed).

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read the file at the referenced path. The user will normally pass the path or the issue number directly.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a file with one **child** file per ticket.

- **Map**: `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` (the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body).
- **Child ticket**: `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, with the question in the body. A `Type:` line records the ticket type (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`); a `Status:` line records `claimed`/`resolved`.
- **Blocking**: a `Blocked by: NN, NN` line near the top. A ticket is unblocked when every file it lists is `resolved`.
- **Frontier**: scan `.scratch/<effort>/issues/` for files that are open, unblocked, and unclaimed; first by number wins.
- **Claim**: set `Status: claimed` and save before any work.
- **Resolve**: append the answer under an `## Answer` heading, set `Status: resolved`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far in `map.md`.

# Issue tracker: Local Markdown

Issues and specs for this repo live as markdown files in `.scratch/`.

## Conventions

- One feature per directory: `.scratch/<feature-slug>/`
- The spec is `.scratch/<feature-slug>/spec.md`
- Implementation issues are one file per ticket at `.scratch/<feature-slug>/issues/<NN>-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, never a single combined tickets file
- Triage state is recorded as a `Status:` line near the top of each issue file (see `triage-labels.md` for the role strings)
- Comments and conversation history append to the bottom of the file under a `## Comments` heading

## When a skill says "publish to the issue tracker"

Create a new file under `.scratch/<feature-slug>/` (creating the directory if needed).

## When a skill says "fetch the relevant ticket"

Read the file at the referenced path. The user will normally pass the path or the issue number directly.

## Wayfinding operations

Used by `/wayfinder`. The **map** is a file with one **child** file per ticket.

- **Map**: `.scratch/<effort>/map.md` (the Notes / Decisions-so-far / Fog body).
- **Child ticket**: `.scratch/<effort>/issues/NN-<slug>.md`, numbered from `01`, with the question in the body. A `Type:` line records the ticket type (`research`/`prototype`/`grilling`/`task`); a `Status:` line records `claimed`/`resolved`.
- **Blocking**: a `Blocked by: NN, NN` line near the top. A ticket is unblocked when every file it lists is `resolved`.
- **Frontier**: scan `.scratch/<effort>/issues/` for files that are open, unblocked, and unclaimed; first by number wins.
- **Claim**: set `Status: claimed` and save before any work.
- **Resolve**: append the answer under an `## Answer` heading, set `Status: resolved`, then append a context pointer (gist + link) to the map's Decisions-so-far in `map.md`.

#!/bin/bash
# Checks the commit criteria of the tickets in a separate clone.
# Part A: the full test suite at each refactor commit of Phase 1 and at each later refactor commit.
# Part B: for each fix commit that changes API tests, the tests pass at the commit and fail on its parent.
REPO=/Users/aesbetancourt/Dev/personal/interviews/treatwell/ai-engineer-take-home
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
CLONE="$HERE/clone"
OUT="$HERE/result.txt"
LOG="$HERE/log.txt"
: > "$OUT"
: > "$LOG"

if [ ! -d "$CLONE/.git" ]; then
  git clone -q "$REPO" "$CLONE" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
fi
cd "$CLONE" || exit 1

goto() {
  git reset -q --hard >> "$LOG" 2>&1
  git checkout -q -f "$1" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
  yarn install --immutable >> "$LOG" 2>&1 || echo "INSTALL FAILED at $1" >> "$OUT"
}

echo "== A: yarn test at each commit" >> "$OUT"
for c in f75dd8a a99548f 211698d 4a4f10d c055f28 be30460 94a22e4 10b25d9 7e7e048 1444bb1 dabfb22 201d6b5; do
  goto "$c"
  echo "--- A $c" >> "$LOG"
  if yarn test >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then r=green; else r=RED; fi
  echo "$c $r $(git log -1 --format=%s "$c")" >> "$OUT"
done

echo "== B: tests of each fix commit, at the commit and on its parent" >> "$OUT"
for c in $(git log --reverse --format=%h --grep='^fix:' main); do
  files=$(git diff --name-only "$c~1" "$c" -- apps/api/test)
  if [ -z "$files" ]; then
    echo "$c no-api-test $(git log -1 --format=%s "$c")" >> "$OUT"
    continue
  fi
  tests=$(echo "$files" | grep '\.test\.ts$' | sed 's#^apps/api/##' | tr '\n' ' ')
  goto "$c"
  echo "--- B at $c: $tests" >> "$LOG"
  if yarn workspace @venue/api vitest run $tests >> "$LOG" 2>&1; then at=green; else at=RED; fi
  goto "$c~1"
  git checkout -q "$c" -- $files >> "$LOG" 2>&1
  echo "--- B before $c: $tests" >> "$LOG"
  if yarn workspace @venue/api vitest run $tests > "$HERE/before-$c.txt" 2>&1; then before=GREEN; else before=red; fi
  cat "$HERE/before-$c.txt" >> "$LOG"
  failed=$(grep -E '^\s*Tests ' "$HERE/before-$c.txt" | tr -s ' ')
  echo "$c at=$at before=$before [$failed] $(git log -1 --format=%s "$c")" >> "$OUT"
done
echo "== done" >> "$OUT"

1	# NOTES
2	
3	## What did you decide, and why?
4	
5	- **Unknown query parameters return 400 on `GET /appointments`**, the old `date` included. The brief says the new parameters replace the date filter and that any other value returns 400.
6	- **Legacy appointments are normalised in responses.** `startsAt` is UTC ISO and the status is `cancelled`. The README says the API uses ISO 8601 in UTC, and the legacy format is a storage detail. `createdAt` stays an epoch number, because a type change is a shape change.
7	- **Only a change away from `cancelled` is blocked (409).** The README says an appointment "normally" goes pending → confirmed → completed, which is not a rule.
8	- **The reminder job claims before it sends.** See `docs/adr/0001-reminder-claim-before-send.md`. The claim also requires the status `confirmed`, so an appointment cancelled a moment before gets no reminder. Two more fixes came with the first test of the job: it read a legacy start time as UTC, so the 24 hour window was off by the venue offset, and the email stated the start time in server time.
9	- **The confirmation page gets its own BFF route with a public schema.** The API keeps `notes` for staff. The BFF is the boundary to the customer.
10	- **The delete button is on the appointment list.** No appointment detail page exists.
11	- **A new `startsAt` must be ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset, and is stored as UTC.** A string without a zone has no defined instant.
12	- **Staff email is stored as sent, with a unique index on `lower(email)`.** The response then equals the input, and `Anna@x.com` still conflicts with `anna@x.com`. The index rejects the duplicate, so two replicas cannot both insert it. `GET /staff` uses the plain order of the database, so `Zoe` comes before `anna`; the brief says only "ordered by name". The name and the email lose the spaces around them before validation.
13	- **Create and delete audit entries use the update shape**, with `from: null` on create and `to: null` on delete. A `PATCH` that changes no value writes no entry. The values are the ones that the API shows, so a legacy appointment has a UTC start time and the status `cancelled` in its trail. A seeded appointment has no create entry: its trail is empty until the first change. The seed clears the audit table, because it gives the appointments their ids again.
14	- **One direct test proves the shared transaction.** It removes the audit table from a temporary database and calls the service: the create, the update and the delete each fail and leave no change. No endpoint can make the audit write fail.
15	- **The API never runs migrations on start.** The `dev` script runs `db:migrate` first. Seed-on-boot is off when `NODE_ENV=production`. The API also does not stop when the schema is behind: it starts and answers 500 on a route that needs a missing table. Tests start real processes and read the database file to prove each point. Two effects: a migration that is generated while `yarn dev` runs needs a `yarn db:migrate` by hand, and a production start on a missing database still makes an empty file, with no table.
16	- **The API image runs `tsx`**, the same path the tests use. A compile step is the next move before real production. I built both images and ran them together: `db:migrate` two times, the API with a key, and the web image against it. The API container reports healthy and stops with exit code 0. The first web build failed, because the image did not hold `tsconfig.base.json`; the build check found it. The web install needs more than 2 GB of memory at build time.
17	- **A generated column, `starts_at_utc`, holds the UTC start time.** One SQL expression serves the sort, the date filter, the overlap check and the response. See `docs/adr/0002-generated-column-for-start-time.md`. A sweep of 1.2 million local times from 2020 to 2040 against the time zone database found no difference. The hour that does not exist in March and the hour that occurs twice in October are read as summer time.
18	- **`from` later than `to` returns 200 with empty items.** Each value is valid, and the brief states no rule for the pair.
19	- **The list query is strict.** `page=1e1`, `page=1.5`, an empty value, a parameter given twice, `status=canceled` and the old `date` return 400. Each sort has the id as the last key, in the same direction, so two pages never show the same appointment and `desc` is the exact reverse of `asc`. The page and the total come from one read transaction. An unknown parameter returns 400 too; the brief says "any other value", and I read it to include a parameter name.
20	- **A legacy appointment at a day boundary has a direct test.** The API cannot create a legacy appointment, and the seed has none near midnight. The test writes them to a temporary database and calls the service.
21	- **`db:check` runs `drizzle-kit generate` on a temporary copy of the migrations folder** and fails when a new file appears. `drizzle-kit check` does not read `schema.ts`, and `generate` always exits with 0. The check uses the same command as `db:generate`, so the two cannot disagree. A renamed column or table fails the check too: drizzle-kit asks a question about a rename, and the check gives it no terminal, so it reports no clear result.
22	- **Two tests start two API processes on one database.** One sends the same appointment to both, the other moves two appointments to the same time. Without the immediate transaction both tests fail in each run, with two accepted appointments. With a deferred transaction they fail with 500. One process cannot show this race.
23	- **Tests call a function directly only when no endpoint exists**: the reminder job and the daylight-saving conversion.
24	- **Four small hardening changes**: no appointment request body in the logs (the refactor removed it), `busy_timeout` and WAL, a clean stop on `SIGTERM`, and `GET /health`. On `SIGTERM` the API takes no new request, lets each open request finish, and exits with code 0. `GET /health` needs no API key and does not read the database.
25	
26	## What I found in the appointments web pages
27	
28	| Finding | Action |
29	|---|---|
30	| The BFF always returns 200, so a 409 looks like success | The BFF forwards the status code of the API (`fix`) |
31	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` ships the API key to the browser | The API URL and the key come from server-only environment variables |
32	| The Overview page calls the API directly | The Overview page calls a new BFF summary route |
33	| The create form closes whatever the result | The form shows the error and stays open (`fix`) |
34	| The status filter sends `canceled`, so it shows only legacy appointments | The filter sends `cancelled` (`fix`) |
35	| Times display in browser time, and the form reads the start time as browser time | Times display in venue time (Europe/Berlin), and the form reads the start time as venue time (`fix`) |
36	| The BFF sends any body and any id to the API, so `..%2Fcustomers` as an id reaches another API route | The appointment BFF handlers parse the body with the contract and accept digits only as an id |
37	
38	## What did you skip, and why?
39	
40	- **The BFF handlers of customers and treatments.** They still answer 200 for each API status. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
41	- **The same rule for a special hour in the form and in legacy data.** In the hour that occurs twice in October, the form reads winter time and a legacy appointment reads summer time. The venue is closed at 02:30.
42	- **The log of the customer request body.** `POST /customers` still prints the name, the email and the phone. The brief limits the work to appointments.
43	- **An edit form for a staff member.** The API and the BFF can change one, and the page only lists and creates. The brief asks for a list page and a create form.
44	- **A rollout plan for the new list contract.** `GET /appointments` changes its response shape and drops `date` in one release. During a rolling update, a web replica of the previous version gets a shape it cannot read. A versioned route, or a web release that reads both shapes first, closes this window.
45	- **Error bodies of customers and treatments.** They keep their four shapes. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
46	- **Signed links for the confirmation page.** Appointment ids are sequential, so anyone can read a booking by its id. The page now gets only the name, the treatment, the time, the price and the status.
47	- **A browser check of the list controls.** The URL state has no automated test. I checked the production build, the page with a full query string, and the BFF answers. I did not click the controls in a browser.
48	- **A test runner for the web app.** No automated test calls a BFF route or a page. The confirmation fix has a test for the public schema, and the venue time fix has a test for the conversion. The three other web fixes have no test that fails before them; I checked them by hand with requests that the API rejects.
49	- **The same error order in the BFF and the API.** For an unknown id with an invalid body, `PATCH` answers 400 in the BFF and 404 in the API, because the BFF parses the body first.
50	- **Authentication in the web app.** The staff BFF route `/api/appointments/:id` still returns `notes` to anyone who has the URL. The confirmation page no longer calls it.
51	- **An outbox for reminders.** A crash between the claim and the send loses one reminder. So does a send that the email provider rejects, because the job does not retry.
52	- **A two-release rollout for soft delete.** During a rolling update, the previous version still shows a deleted appointment and still counts it in the overlap check. See `docs/migrations.md`.
53	- **A data migration for legacy start times.** The stored values stay as they are. A rewrite of customer data cannot be rolled back.
54	- **The SQL injection in `GET /customers?search=`.** The route still builds its SQL from the `search` value with `sql.raw`. The brief limits the work to appointments. This is the first fix before the API goes live.
55	- **The error body of the API key check.** A request with no key or a wrong key gets 401 with `{ error: 'Unauthorized' }`. The check came with the repo and answers in a hook, so the error handler does not make this body. The contract has no code for it. My plan did not cover it.
56	- **A new reminder for a moved appointment.** A change of the start time keeps the reminder mark. An appointment that moves after its reminder gets no reminder for the new time. No test covers this. A fix clears the mark when the start time changes.
57	- **The customer cache of the appointments page.** The module-level `customerCache` came with the repo and nothing clears it. A customer that is created after the first load is absent from the create form until a reload. A status change that the API rejects also shows no message; the list only loads again.
58	
59	## Behaviour that changed outside a `fix` commit
60	
61	The appointments refactor keeps the status code and the body for each valid input. A differential run sent the same 150 requests to the old and the new code to check this. These responses to invalid input changed:
62	
63	| Input | Before | After |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| SQL in the `status` or `date` filter | 200 with all appointments, or 500 | 200 with an empty list |
66	| A filter sent twice (`?status=a&status=b`) | 200 with an empty list | 400 |
67	| `customerId` or `treatmentId` that is not a positive integer (`-1`, `1.5`, `"1"`, `[1]`, `true`) | 201, 404 or 500 | 400 |
68	| `notes` that is not a string or `null` | accepted, or 500 | 400 |
69	| An appointment whose customer or treatment row is missing (not run; the seed has none) | 200 with a partial item, or 500 | absent from the list, 404 on read and update |
70	| The reminder job meets an appointment whose customer row is missing | The job throws, and sends no later reminder in that run | The job skips that appointment |
71	
72	Two more changes have no effect on a response:
73	
74	- **The in-memory booking lock is gone.** The service is now synchronous, so one process cannot interleave two bookings. The rule across replicas is a separate fix.
75	- **A booking is one insert with the real price.** Before, it was an insert with price 0 and then an update.
76	
77	## Characterization tests that changed
78	
79	Each change is its own commit.
80	
81	| Test | Before | After | Reason |
82	|---|---|---|---|
83	| `POST /appointments` "an appointment that starts as another one ends" | 409 | 201 | The README says back-to-back is fine. The test recorded a bug. |
84	| The six `GET /appointments` tests ("returns every appointment with its customer and treatment", "orders ISO-timestamped appointments by start time", "computes endsAt from the treatment duration", "filters by status", "filters by date", "combines the status and date filters") | They read an array and use `?date=` | They read `items` and use `?from=&to=`; two also check `total` | The brief replaces the list contract. The expected appointments are the same. |
85	| The helper `helpers/server.ts` | No `delete` method | A `delete` method | The tests of `DELETE /appointments/:id` need it. No test in the folder changed. |
86	
87	## What `yarn verify` still reports
88	
89	Five of seven checks pass: both typechecks, jscpd, `db:check` and the tests. Two fail, and each finding is in code that came with the repo. I left that code as it is, because the brief limits the work to appointments.
90	
91	| Check | Finding | Where |
92	|---|---|---|
93	| ESLint | 18 errors: `any`, and two unused `reply` parameters | `apps/api/src/routes.ts`, the customers and treatments routes |
94	| ESLint | 1 error: `any` | `apps/web/app/treatments/page.tsx` |
95	| knip | The unused file `apps/api/src/utils/legacy.ts` | Its own comment says that nothing imports it |
96	| knip | The unused packages `lodash`, `@types/lodash` and `dayjs` | The two `package.json` files |
97	
98	The appointments module, the staff module, the contract package and the tests have no ESLint error. The mapper has its own `toStatus` and does not use `legacyStatus` from the unused file, because that one returns a plain `string` and not the status type of the contract.
99	
100	## Where did the AI get something wrong, and how did you catch it?
101	
102	- **Legacy `startsAt` in responses.** The AI first advised to return it as stored, to keep "today's shape". A second read of the README rule and of the ordering test, which skips legacy rows, showed that normalisation is correct.
103	
104	- **Staff order without regard to letter case.** The AI ordered `GET /staff` with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The brief says "ordered by name", and its tests run against that contract. A review flagged the addition, and the plain order replaced it.
105	
106	- **Loose ids in the routes.** The AI read each path id with `Number`, as the original code did. A review probed `DELETE /appointments/1e0`, and it deleted appointment 1. The routes now read the id with the id schema of the contract, and tests cover `1e0`, `0x1` and `1.0`.
107	
108	- **Staff email in lower case.** The AI-written plan stored the email in lower case. A response would then differ from the input. The index on `lower(email)` gives the same uniqueness and keeps the value.
109	
110	## What would you do next with another day?
111	
112	- **i18n.** The pages and the error messages hold English text in the code.
113	- **Import aliases.** The web handlers use paths such as `../../../../../lib/api`. An alias such as `@/lib/api` removes them.
114	- **oxlint and oxfmt in place of ESLint.** They run faster, so each check in the edit loop costs less. The repo has no formatter today.
115	- **Husky with pre-commit hooks.** Lint, typecheck and `db:check` run before each commit, not only in `yarn verify`.
116	- **CASL, if the app gets roles.** Today each caller with the API key can do all actions. With roles, one set of ability rules serves the API and the pages.
117	- **`@fastify/error` in place of the custom error classes.** It gives each error a code and a status in the way Fastify expects.
118	
119	## What would you want in place before this goes live?
120	
121	- A database that is not one SQLite file. The booking transaction takes the write lock of the whole database, a replica that waits for it blocks its event loop for up to 5 seconds and then returns 500, and WAL mode needs all replicas on one host.
122	
123	- Foreign keys, indexes and constraints on the three original tables.
124	- Mandatory authentication, and a CORS setting that is not `*`.
125	- Money as integer cents, not `REAL`.
126	- A readiness check that fails when the schema is behind the code, so the platform sends no request to that replica.
127	- A guard on `db:seed`. The script is in the production image, and it replaces all data. It has no guard, because the tests of the brief run it and I do not know their `NODE_ENV`.
128	- A pinned base image (a digest in place of `node:22-slim`), and a volume that Kubernetes mounts with the right owner.
129	- A clean stop for the web image. The Next server exits on `SIGTERM` with code 143 and does not wait for an open request.
130	- A structured logger.
131	- An outbox with retry for reminders.
132	- Signed links for the customer confirmation page.
133	- A compile step for the API image.

Two effects: a migration that is generated while `yarn dev` runs needs a `yarn db:migrate` by hand, and a production start on a missing database still makes an empty file, with no table.
- **The API image runs `tsx`**, the same path the tests use. A compile step is the next move before real production. I built both images and ran them together: `db:migrate` two times, the API with a key, and the web image against it. The API container reports healthy and stops with exit code 0. The first web build failed, because the image did not hold `tsconfig.base.json`; the build check found it. The web install needs more than 2 GB of memory at build time.
- **A generated column, `starts_at_utc`, holds the UTC start time.** One SQL expression serves the sort, the date filter, the overlap check and the response. See `docs/adr/0002-generated-column-for-start-time.md`. A sweep of 1.2 million local times from 2020 to 2040 against the time zone database found no difference. The hour that does not exist in March and the hour that occurs twice in October are read as summer time.
- **`from` later than `to` returns 200 with empty items.** Each value is valid, and the brief states no rule for the pair.
- **The list query is strict.** `page=1e1`, `page=1.5`, an empty value, a parameter given twice, `status=canceled` and the old `date` return 400. Each sort has the id as the last key, in the same direction, so two pages never show the same appointment and `desc` is the exact reverse of `asc`. The page and the total come from one read transaction. An unknown parameter returns 400 too; the brief says "any other value", and I read it to include a parameter name.
- **A legacy appointment at a day boundary has a direct test.** The API cannot create a legacy appointment, and the seed has none near midnight. The test writes them to a temporary database and calls the service.
- **`db:check` runs `drizzle-kit generate` on a temporary copy of the migrations folder** and fails when a new file appears. `drizzle-kit check` does not read `schema.ts`, and `generate` always exits with 0. The check uses the same command as `db:generate`, so the two cannot disagree. A renamed column or table fails the check too: drizzle-kit asks a question about a rename, and the check gives it no terminal, so it reports no clear result.
- **Two tests start two API processes on one database.** One sends the same appointment to both, the other moves two appointments to the same time. Without the immediate transaction both tests fail in each run, with two accepted appointments. With a deferred transaction they fail with 500. One process cannot show this race.
- **Tests call a function directly only when no endpoint exists**: the reminder job and the daylight-saving conversion.
- **Four small hardening changes**: no appointment request body in the logs (the refactor removed it), `busy_timeout` and WAL, a clean stop on `SIGTERM`, and `GET /health`. On `SIGTERM` the API takes no new request, lets each open request finish, and exits with code 0. `GET /health` needs no API key and does not read the database.

## What I found in the appointments web pages

| Finding | Action |
|---|---|
| The BFF always returns 200, so a 409 looks like success | The BFF forwards the status code of the API (`fix`) |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` ships the API key to the browser | The API URL and the key come from server-only environment variables |
| The Overview page calls the API directly | The Overview page calls a new BFF summary route |
| The create form closes whatever the result | The form shows the error and stays open (`fix`) |
| The status filter sends `canceled`, so it shows only legacy appointments | The filter sends `cancelled` (`fix`) |
| Times display in browser time, and the form reads the start time as browser time | Times display in venue time (Europe/Berlin), and the form reads the start time as venue time (`fix`) |
| The BFF sends any body and any id to the API, so `..%2Fcustomers` as an id reaches another API route | The appointment BFF handlers parse the body with the contract and accept digits only as an id |

## What did you skip, and why?

- **The BFF handlers of customers and treatments.** They still answer 200 for each API status. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
- **The same rule for a special hour in the form and in legacy data.** In the hour that occurs twice in October, the form reads winter time and a legacy appointment reads summer time. The venue is closed at 02:30.
- **The log of the customer request body.** `POST /customers` still prints the name, the email and the phone. The brief limits the work to appointments.
- **An edit form for a staff member.** The API and the BFF can change one, and the page only lists and creates. The brief asks for a list page and a create form.
- **A rollout plan for the new list contract.** `GET /appointments` changes its response shape and drops `date` in one release. During a rolling update, a web replica of the previous version gets a shape it cannot read. A versioned route, or a web release that reads both shapes first, closes this window.
- **Error bodies of customers and treatments.** They keep their four shapes. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
- **Signed links for the confirmation page.** Appointment ids are sequential, so anyone can read a booking by its id. The page now gets only the name, the treatment, the time, the price and the status.
- **A browser check of the list controls.** The URL state has no automated test. I checked the production build, the page with a full query string, and the BFF answers. I did not click the controls in a browser.
- **A test runner for the web app.** No automated test calls a BFF route or a page. The confirmation fix has a test for the public schema, and the venue time fix has a test for the conversion. The three other web fixes have no test that fails before them; I checked them by hand with requests that the API rejects.
- **The same error order in the BFF and the API.** For an unknown id with an invalid body, `PATCH` answers 400 in the BFF and 404 in the API, because the BFF parses the body first.
- **Authentication in the web app.** The staff BFF route `/api/appointments/:id` still returns `notes` to anyone who has the URL. The confirmation page no longer calls it.
- **An outbox for reminders.** A crash between the claim and the send loses one reminder. So does a send that the email provider rejects, because the job does not retry.
- **A two-release rollout for soft delete.** During a rolling update, the previous version still shows a deleted appointment and still counts it in the overlap check. See `docs/migrations.md`.
- **A data migration for legacy start times.** The stored values stay as they are. A rewrite of customer data cannot be rolled back.
- **The SQL injection in `GET /customers?search=`.** The route still builds its SQL from the `search` value with `sql.raw`. The brief limits the work to appointments. This is the first fix before the API goes live.
- **The error body of the API key check.** A request with no key or a wrong key gets 401 with `{ error: 'Unauthorized' }`. The check came with the repo and answers in a hook, so the error handler does not make this body. The contract has no code for it. My plan did not cover it.
- **A new reminder for a moved appointment.** A change of the start time keeps the reminder mark. An appointment that moves after its reminder gets no reminder for the new time. No test covers this. A fix clears the mark when the start time changes.
- **The customer cache of the appointments page.** The module-level `customerCache` came with the repo and nothing clears it. A customer that is created after the first load is absent from the create form until a reload. A status change that the API rejects also shows no message; the list only loads again.

## Behaviour that changed outside a `fix` commit

The appointments refactor keeps the status code and the body for each valid input. A differential run sent the same 150 requests to the old and the new code to check this. These responses to invalid input changed:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| SQL in the `status` or `date` filter | 200 with all appointments, or 500 | 200 with an empty list |
| A filter sent twice (`?status=a&status=b`) | 200 with an empty list | 400 |
| `customerId` or `treatmentId` that is not a positive integer (`-1`, `1.5`, `"1"`, `[1]`, `true`) | 201, 404 or 500 | 400 |
| `notes` that is not a string or `null` | accepted, or 500 | 400 |
| An appointment whose customer or treatment row is missing (not run; the seed has none) | 200 with a partial item, or 500 | absent from the list, 404 on read and update |
| The reminder job meets an appointment whose customer row is missing | The job throws, and sends no later reminder in that run | The job skips that appointment |

Two more changes have no effect on a response:

- **The in-memory booking lock is gone.** The service is now synchronous, so one process cannot interleave two bookings. The rule across replicas is a separate fix.
- **A booking is one insert with the real price.** Before, it was an insert with price 0 and then an update.

## Characterization tests that changed

Each change is its own commit.

| Test | Before | After | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /appointments` "an appointment that starts as another one ends" | 409 | 201 | The README says back-to-back is fine. The test recorded a bug. |
| The six `GET /appointments` tests ("returns every appointment with its customer and treatment", "orders ISO-timestamped appointments by start time", "computes endsAt from the treatment duration", "filters by status", "filters by date", "combines the status and date filters") | They read an array and use `?date=` | They read `items` and use `?from=&to=`; two also check `total` | The brief replaces the list contract. The expected appointments are the same. |
| The helper `helpers/server.ts` | No `delete` method | A `delete` method | The tests of `DELETE /appointments/:id` need it. No test in the folder changed. |

## What `yarn verify` still reports

Five of seven checks pass: both typechecks, jscpd, `db:check` and the tests. Two fail, and each finding is in code that came with the repo. I left that code as it is, because the brief limits the work to appointments.

| Check | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|
| ESLint | 18 errors: `any`, and two unused `reply` parameters | `apps/api/src/routes.ts`, the customers and treatments routes |
| ESLint | 1 error: `any` | `apps/web/app/treatments/page.tsx` |
| knip | The unused file `apps/api/src/utils/legacy.ts` | Its own comment says that nothing imports it |
| knip | The unused packages `lodash`, `@types/lodash` and `dayjs` | The two `package.json` files |

The appointments module, the staff module, the contract package and the tests have no ESLint error. The mapper has its own `toStatus` and does not use `legacyStatus` from the unused file, because that one returns a plain `string` and not the status type of the contract.

## Where did the AI get something wrong, and how did you catch it?

- **Legacy `startsAt` in responses.** The AI first advised to return it as stored, to keep "today's shape". A second read of the README rule and of the ordering test, which skips legacy rows, showed that normalisation is correct.

- **Staff order without regard to letter case.** The AI ordered `GET /staff` with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The brief says "ordered by name", and its tests run against that contract. A review flagged the addition, and the plain order replaced it.

- **Loose ids in the routes.** The AI read each path id with `Number`, as the original code did. A review probed `DELETE /appointments/1e0`, and it deleted appointment 1. The routes now read the id with the id schema of the contract, and tests cover `1e0`, `0x1` and `1.0`.

- **Staff email in lower case.** The AI-written plan stored the email in lower case. A response would then differ from the input. The index on `lower(email)` gives the same uniqueness and keeps the value.

## What would you do next with another day?

- **i18n.** The pages and the error messages hold English text in the code.
- **Import aliases.** The web handlers use paths such as `../../../../../lib/api`. An alias such as `@/lib/api` removes them.
- **oxlint and oxfmt in place of ESLint.** They run faster, so each check in the edit loop costs less. The repo has no formatter today.
- **Husky with pre-commit hooks.** Lint, typecheck and `db:check` run before each commit, not only in `yarn verify`.
- **CASL, if the app gets roles.** Today each caller with the API key can do all actions. With roles, one set of ability rules serves the API and the pages.
- **`@fastify/error` in place of the custom error classes.** It gives each error a code and a status in the way Fastify expects.

## What would you want in place before this goes live?

- A database that is not one SQLite file. The booking transaction takes the write lock of the whole database, a replica that waits for it blocks its event loop for up to 5 seconds and then returns 500, and WAL mode needs all replicas on one host.

- Foreign keys, indexes and constraints on the three original tables.
- Mandatory authentication, and a CORS setting that is not `*`.
- Money as integer cents, not `REAL`.
- A readiness check that fails when the schema is behind the code, so the platform sends no request to that replica.
- A guard on `db:seed`. The script is in the production image, and it replaces all data. It has no guard, because the tests of the brief run it and I do not know their `NODE_ENV`.
- A pinned base image (a digest in place of `node:22-slim`), and a volume that Kubernetes mounts with the right owner.
- A clean stop for the web image. The Next server exits on `SIGTERM` with code 143 and does not wait for an open request.
- A structured logger.
- An outbox with retry for reminders.
- Signed links for the customer confirmation page.
- A compile step for the API image.

FROM node:22-slim AS build

RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare yarn@4.18.1 --activate
WORKDIR /app
# The package files come first, so a code change does not install the dependencies again.
COPY package.json yarn.lock .yarnrc.yml ./
COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY apps/web/package.json apps/web/
COPY packages/contract/package.json packages/contract/
RUN yarn workspaces focus @venue/web

COPY packages/contract packages/contract

# The standalone output holds the server and only the dependencies that it uses.

COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/web/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=build --chown=node:node /app/apps/web/.next/static ./apps/web/.next/static

EXPOSE 3000
# The image has no curl, so node makes the request. The overview page needs no API call on the server.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=10s --timeout=3s --start-period=10s --retries=3 \
  CMD node -e "fetch('http://127.0.0.1:' + process.env.PORT + '/').then((r) => process.exit(r.ok ? 0 : 1)).catch(() => process.exit(1))"
CMD ["node", "apps/web/server.js"]

# Each replica:              docker run -p 4000:4000 -v venue-data:/data -e API_KEY=... venue-api
# See docs/migrations.md.

FROM node:22-slim AS base
# Yarn comes from corepack. This directory holds it, so the non-root user needs no download at run time.
ENV COREPACK_HOME=/opt/corepack
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare yarn@4.18.1 --activate && chmod -R a+rX /opt/corepack
WORKDIR /app

# Production dependencies only. The package files come first, so a code change does not install them again.
FROM base AS deps
# better-sqlite3 has a native part. These tools build it when no prebuilt binary fits. They stay in this stage.

COPY apps/api/package.json apps/api/
COPY apps/web/package.json apps/web/
COPY packages/contract/package.json packages/contract/
RUN yarn workspaces focus @venue/api --production

   - Git commits denied (tickets 01, 02 and later), `git checkout -- …` denied, a compound scratch command with `rm -rf`/`pkill` denied: I stopped committing; the user commits.    - Ticket 01: the user committed `contract.test.ts` (with an error-body test needing the handler) in the first commit and `yarn.lock` with the web entry before `apps/web/package.json`; history cannot be rewritten; later fixed by a `chore` commit for the web wiring.
   - errors.ts: I replaced classes with functions on a soft remark; user chose the original classes; restored. Lesson saved in memory.
   - I put a new test file in the characterization folder; user: "I would not like to touch the original characterization folder"; moved to `apps/api/test/appointments-edges.test.ts`.
   - I ran `git stash` by mistake in ticket 02; restored with `git stash pop` in the next command; told the user.
   - Ticket 02 review: one injection test passed on old code (changed to a quote in `date`); NOTES table incomplete/wrong (rewritten by input class).
   - Ticket 03 review: `lib/api.ts` not really server-only → added `server-only` package.
   - Ticket 04 review: glossary word "slot" → `OverlapCheck`; hole (cancelled → confirmed revive) closed in ticket 05.
   - Ticket 05 review: `PATCH {status:'cancelled'}` rewrote stored `canceled` → status no longer written for an already cancelled appointment; empty update guarded.
   - Ticket 06: Fastify `setErrorHandler` error typed `unknown` earlier required `FastifyError` annotation; null `starts_at_utc` returned raw value → mapper converts in TypeScript; reminder window fix moved to ticket 08.
   - Ticket 07 review: added PATCH race test, body assertion, pragma order swap, lookups inside the transaction; confirmed the reviewer claim "old version gets SQLITE_BUSY at once" was wrong (better-sqlite3 default timeout 5000).
   - A sentence of mine joined two facts ("CLAUDE.md requires: … is two statements"); clarified on request.

5. Problem Solving:
   - Resolved brief ambiguities by decision (23 grilling answers, all accepted): unknown query params → 400; legacy `startsAt` and status normalised in responses, `createdAt` stays epoch ms; delete button on the list; Phase 1 keeps 200 for unknown status; error handler covers thrown and Fastify errors only; contract in `packages/contract`; only leaving `cancelled` is blocked; reminder claims before send; confirmation page gets a public BFF schema; strict ISO input; generated column; staff email stored as sent with `lower(email)` unique index; audit entries use `{from,to}` for all actions; web fixes; no migrate on start, no seed in production; `tsx` at runtime in the image; `from` > `to` → 200 empty; accept soft-delete rollout window; no data migration for legacy start times; direct tests only without an endpoint; two-process test; four hardening items; `db:check` approach A.
   - Tickets 01–06 are committed by the user (HEAD at start of ticket 07 was `12290e2 fix: require a zone in startsAt and store it in UTC`; tag `phase-1-refactor` exists). Ticket 07 is implemented, reviewed, green (114 tests; both replica tests fail without the transaction), and uncommitted.
=== summary 2 ===

   - Compound commands with `rm -rf`, `pkill`, `docker rm -f`, `docker rm`/`volume rm` were denied: I split commands and avoided removals; Docker leftovers remain.
   - Ticket 08: `Intl` output differs by ICU version → loosened the assertion; review found the ADR claim "missed only on a crash" was wrong → corrected ADR 0001 and NOTES.
   - Ticket 09: review → added status assertion, replaced the word "booking", route returns fixed errors only.
   - Ticket 10: zsh did not split `$J` header variable (false 400s) → fixed the curl helper; review → `errorResponse` options object, confirmation route 502, form error handling.
   - Ticket 12: I used `COLLATE NOCASE` for staff order; review flagged risk with external tests → plain order (`17aec28`), recorded as AI mistake.
   - Ticket 13/16: ids read with `Number` (`1e0` reached record 1; `DELETE /appointments/1e0` deleted appointment 1) → shared `toId` helper with contract schema; DELETE with JSON content type and no body returned 400 → content-type dropped on DELETE.
   - Ticket 14: review → list+count in one read transaction, id tiebreak follows direction; commit `769901a` bundles two fixes (admitted, cannot rewrite). Ticket 15 commit `ff7f535` also bundles several small fixes.
   - Ticket 19: test first ran the fix on an empty table → rewritten to migrate to pre-fix schema, add rows, then migrate.
   - Ticket 20: rename gave only a stack trace → clearer message; ESLint console warnings → file-level disable comment.
   - Ticket 21: Docker daemon not running → started colima; web build OOM-killed in the 2 GiB default VM (kernel log confirmed 1.78 GB) → temporary profile `venue-build` with 4 GiB, deleted after; web build failed because `tsconfig.base.json` was not copied → added to both Dockerfiles. Commit `89ab2fd` (web HEALTHCHECK, `.dockerignore`) was not rebuilt.
   - Ticket 22: fact check found "each migration only adds" false and other overstatements → corrected.
   - I said "two-agent review" for ticket 18 but used one agent; stated the correction.
   - User feedback: reviews make tickets slow → I offered options A–D; user enabled commits (D); I used one short agent for small tickets and two agents for 14, 16, 17.

5. Problem Solving:
   All of tickets 08–22 are implemented, reviewed and committed (74 commits on `main`; last code/doc commit `492dbb7 docs: correct docs/migrations.md after a fact check`). `yarn verify`: 5 of 7 pass; ESLint (20 errors in `apps/api/src/routes.ts` and `apps/web/app/treatments/page.tsx`) and knip (unused `utils/legacy.ts`, `lodash`, `@types/lodash`, `dayjs`) fail in code from the initial commit; the user decided to leave them and note them. Tags present: `phase-1-refactor`, `phase-1-fixes`, `phase-2-features` (no Phase 3 tag yet).

#!/bin/bash
# Starts the API before the refactor (4a4f10d) and after it (94a22e4), each on its own database,
# and sends the same requests to both. Stops both servers at the end.
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aesbetancourt-Dev-personal-interviews-treatwell-ai-engineer-take-home/9fbffbed-3a36-4b27-83e4-27fabc3b1389/scratchpad
H=$S/history-check
T=$S/ticket-23
SCRIPT=${1:-$S/diff.mjs}

start() { # dir port name
  (cd "$1/apps/api" && TZ=UTC PORT=$2 DB_PATH="$T/$3.db" yarn tsx src/index.ts > "$T/$3.log" 2>&1) &
}
# A new database for each run.
: > "$T/old.db.marker"
for n in old new; do for x in "" -shm -wal; do [ -f "$T/$n.db$x" ] && mv "$T/$n.db$x" "$T/$n.db$x.$(date +%s)"; done; done

start "$H/old" 4101 old
OLD=$!
start "$H/clone" 4102 new
NEW=$!
for p in 4101 4102; do
  for i in $(seq 1 80); do curl -s -o /dev/null "localhost:$p/treatments" && break; sleep 0.25; done
done
node "$SCRIPT"
# Stop the servers that this script started.
for p in 4101 4102; do
  pid=$(lsof -tiTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN)
  [ -n "$pid" ] && kill $pid
done
wait $OLD $NEW 2>/dev/null
echo "listeners left: $(lsof -tiTCP:4101 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l | tr -d ' ') $(lsof -tiTCP:4102 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"

1 │ # Venue Backoffice
 2 │ 
 3 │ Welcome, and thanks for taking the time to do this exercise.
 4 │ 
 5 │ This repo is the starting point for your take-home. It's the backoffice a beauty and wellness venue (a salon, spa
 6 │ or barber) uses to run its day: the appointment calendar, its customers and the treatments it offers.
 7 │ 
 8 │ The code works, but it's messy, and that's on purpose. Part of the exercise is deciding what to fix, what to leave
 9 │ alone and how to tell the difference. The brief that came with your invitation describes what we'd like you to
10 │ do. This README covers the repo itself: how to run it, the business rules and how the API is tested.
11 │ 
12 │ ## What's in the repo
13 │ 
14 │ - `apps/api`: the API, in TypeScript with Fastify, Drizzle ORM and SQLite.
15 │ - `apps/web`: the web app, in Next.js (App Router) and React. Its route handlers act as a backend-for-frontend
16 │   (BFF) in front of the API.
17 │ 
18 │ ## Getting started
19 │ 
20 │ ```bash
21 │ corepack enable
22 │ yarn install
23 │ yarn dev        # API on http://localhost:4000, web app on http://localhost:3000
24 │ ```
25 │ 
26 │ You'll find the Node version in `.nvmrc`. The SQLite database is stored in `apps/api/data/`. The dev server
27 │ reloads the sample data every time it starts, so if you want your changes to survive a restart, set
28 │ `SEED_ON_BOOT=false`.
29 │ 
30 │ | Command | What it does |
31 │ | --- | --- |
32 │ | `yarn dev` | Starts the API and the web app |
33 │ | `yarn test` | Runs the API tests, including the characterization suite |
34 │ | `yarn verify` | Runs `tsc`, ESLint, knip, jscpd and the tests, and reports every result |
35 │ | `yarn db:generate` | Generates a Drizzle migration from `apps/api/src/db/schema.ts` |
36 │ | `yarn db:migrate` | Applies pending migrations |
37 │ | `yarn db:seed` | Replaces the data with the sample data |
38 │ 
39 │ Our test suites start the API by running the package scripts `db:migrate`, `db:seed` and `start`, in that order.
40 │ Please keep those three script names working.
41 │ 
42 │ `yarn verify` fails on the starting code, and we expect that. Read its output as a hint about the state of the
43 │ code rather than a gate you have to pass. If you leave something failing, just tell us what and why.
44 │ 
45 │ ## How the venue works
46 │ 
47 │ These are the business rules. If the code and the rules disagree, the rules are right.
48 │ 
49 │ - An **appointment** books one **customer** for one **treatment** at a given start time. It ends when the
50 │   treatment's duration is up. The price, in euros, is copied from the treatment when the appointment is booked.
51 │ - An appointment is `pending`, `confirmed`, `completed` or `cancelled`. It normally goes from pending to confirmed
52 │   to completed. **Cancelling is final**: a cancelled appointment can't be brought back.
53 │ - A customer can't be double-booked, so two of their appointments must never overlap. Back-to-back is fine: one
54 │   can end at 10:30 and the next start at 10:30. **Cancelled appointments don't count.**
55 │ - An appointment's `notes` are for staff only. A customer must never see them.
56 │ - A customer gets **exactly one** reminder email in the 24 hours before a confirmed appointment.
57 │ - The API uses ISO 8601 timestamps in UTC. Appointments imported from the venue's previous booking system are
58 │   different: they are stored as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:mm` in the venue's local time (Europe/Berlin), and some of them
59 │   spell the status `canceled`.
60 │ 
61 │ ## The API contract and the characterization tests
62 │ 
63 │ The tests in `apps/api/test/characterization` record how the API behaves today. Each run starts the real server
64 │ against a freshly seeded database and talks to it only over HTTP, so the tests keep working however you
65 │ reorganise the code inside.
66 │ 
67 │ - For successful requests, both the status code and the response body are part of the contract. For errors,
68 │   only the status code is. Error bodies aren't part of it, and right now they're inconsistent.
69 │ - If you find behaviour that breaks one of the business rules, fix it, but not in the middle of a refactor.
70 │   Make the fix its own commit, with a test that would have caught the bug.
71 │ - The suite is a safety net, not a full specification. Plenty of the code isn't covered.
72 │ - The suite runs the API with `TZ=UTC`, so you'll get the same results on any machine.
73 │ 
74 │ ## How it runs in production
75 │ 
76 │ The backoffice runs on Kubernetes, and each app ships as its own container image.
77 │ 
78 │ - The API and the web app each run as **three replicas** behind a load balancer. Any request can reach any
79 │   replica, and a pod can be stopped or moved at any time.
80 │ - Every merge to `main` goes out as a rolling update, so for a while the old and the new version run side by side.
81 │ - All the API replicas share one database. You'll be working with a local SQLite file, but please treat the
82 │   database as shared and external, the way it is in production.

#!/bin/bash
# Starts the API of the initial commit (4101), the API at HEAD (4102) and the API at HEAD with a key (4103),
# runs probe-head.mjs, and stops the three servers.
S=/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-aesbetancourt-Dev-personal-interviews-treatwell-ai-engineer-take-home/9fbffbed-3a36-4b27-83e4-27fabc3b1389/scratchpad
H=$S/history-check
T=$S/ticket-23
REPO=/Users/aesbetancourt/Dev/personal/interviews/treatwell/ai-engineer-take-home

# A new database for each run.
for n in initial head keyed; do for x in "" -shm -wal; do [ -f "$T/$n.db$x" ] && mv "$T/$n.db$x" "$T/$n.db$x.$(date +%s)"; done; done

(cd "$H/initial/apps/api" && TZ=UTC PORT=4101 DB_PATH="$T/initial.db" yarn tsx src/index.ts > "$T/initial.log" 2>&1) &
P1=$!
(cd "$REPO/apps/api" && export TZ=UTC DB_PATH="$T/head.db" && yarn db:migrate > "$T/head-migrate.log" 2>&1 && yarn db:seed >> "$T/head-migrate.log" 2>&1 && PORT=4102 yarn start > "$T/head.log" 2>&1) &
P2=$!
(cd "$REPO/apps/api" && export TZ=UTC DB_PATH="$T/keyed.db" && yarn db:migrate > /dev/null 2>&1 && yarn db:seed > /dev/null 2>&1 && PORT=4103 API_KEY=secret yarn start > "$T/keyed.log" 2>&1) &
P3=$!
for p in 4101 4102 4103; do
  for i in $(seq 1 120); do curl -s -o /dev/null "localhost:$p/health" && break; sleep 0.25; done
done
node "$T/probe-head.mjs"
for p in 4101 4102 4103; do
  pid=$(lsof -tiTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN)
  [ -n "$pid" ] && kill -TERM $pid
done
wait $P1 $P2 $P3 2>/dev/null
echo
echo "listeners left: $(lsof -tiTCP:4101 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l | tr -d ' ') $(lsof -tiTCP:4102 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l | tr -d ' ') $(lsof -tiTCP:4103 -sTCP:LISTEN | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
echo "--- lines of the HEAD server log that are not request lines:"
grep -v -E '^(GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE) /|^API listening|^\$|^email to' "$T/head.log" | head -20

# The reminder job claims an appointment before it sends the email

The business rule is exactly one reminder per confirmed appointment, and the job runs in each of the three API replicas. The job first claims the appointment with one atomic `UPDATE … WHERE reminder_sent_at IS NULL`, and it sends the email only when that update changed one row. A crash between the claim and the send means the customer gets no reminder. A send that the email provider rejects has the same result, because the job does not release the claim: the provider can fail after it sent the email, and a retry then sends a second one. We accept this, because a second reminder breaks the rule in normal operation, and a missed one happens only on a crash or a failed send.

## Considered options

- **Send, then mark.** Each replica that reads the row before the mark sends an email. This gives duplicates in normal operation.
- **Outbox table with retry.** This gives one reminder and survives a crash. It needs a new table, a worker and an idempotent email provider. It is the correct design for production, and it is out of scope here.
--- tags

content.content:
1	# NOTES
2	
3	## What did you decide, and why?
4	
5	- **Unknown query parameters return 400 on `GET /appointments`**, the old `date` included. The brief says the new parameters replace the date filter and that any other value returns 400.
6	- **Legacy appointments are normalised in responses.** `startsAt` is UTC ISO and the status is `cancelled`. The README says the API uses ISO 8601 in UTC, and the legacy format is a storage detail. `createdAt` stays an epoch number, because a type change is a shape change.
7	- **Only a change away from `cancelled` is blocked (409).** The README says an appointment "normally" goes pending → confirmed → completed, which is not a rule.
8	- **The reminder job claims before it sends.** See `docs/adr/0001-reminder-claim-before-send.md`. The claim also requires the status `confirmed`, so an appointment cancelled a moment before gets no reminder. Two more fixes came with the first test of the job. It read a legacy start time as server time, so on a server that runs in UTC the 24 hour window was off by the venue offset. The email also stated the start time in server time.
9	- **The confirmation page gets its own BFF route with a public schema.** The API keeps `notes` for staff. The BFF is the boundary to the customer.
10	- **The delete button is on the appointment list.** No appointment detail page exists.
11	- **A new `startsAt` must be ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset, and is stored as UTC.** A string without a zone has no defined instant.
12	- **Staff email is stored as sent, with a unique index on `lower(email)`.** The response then equals the input, and `Anna@x.com` still conflicts with `anna@x.com`. The index rejects the duplicate, so two replicas cannot both insert it. `GET /staff` uses the plain order of the database, so `Zoe` comes before `anna`; the brief says only "ordered by name". The test of the order uses three names that sort the same in both orders, so no test fixes this choice. The name and the email lose the spaces around them before validation.
13	- **Create and delete audit entries use the update shape**, with `from: null` on create and `to: null` on delete. A `PATCH` that changes no value writes no entry. The values are the ones that the API shows, so a legacy appointment has a UTC start time and the status `cancelled` in its trail. A seeded appointment has no create entry: its trail is empty until the first change. The seed clears the audit table, because it gives the appointments their ids again.
14	- **One direct test proves the shared transaction.** It removes the audit table from a temporary database and calls the service: the create, the update and the delete each fail and leave no change. No endpoint can make the audit write fail.
15	- **The API never runs migrations on start.** The `dev` script runs `db:migrate` first. Seed-on-boot is off when `NODE_ENV=production`. Tests start the real processes and read the database file: `db:migrate` applies each migration and changes nothing in a second run, a start creates no table, and a production start seeds no data. In production the API also does not stop when the schema is behind: it starts and answers 500 on a route that needs a missing table. I saw this in a run of the image by hand, and no test covers it. Two effects: a migration that is generated while `yarn dev` runs needs a `yarn db:migrate` by hand, and a production start on a missing database still makes an empty file, with no table.
16	- **The API image runs `tsx`**, the same path the tests use. A compile step is the next move before real production. I built both images after the last change to them (`89ab2fd`) and ran them together: `db:migrate` two times, `db:seed`, the API with a key, and the web image against it. Both containers report healthy, and the API container stops with exit code 0. The first web build failed, because the image did not hold `tsconfig.base.json`; the build found it. The web install was killed for lack of memory in a Docker VM with 2 GiB, and it passes with 4 GiB.
17	- **A generated column, `starts_at_utc`, holds the UTC start time.** One SQL expression serves the sort, the date filter, the overlap check and the response. See `docs/adr/0002-generated-column-for-start-time.md`. A sweep of 1.2 million local times from 2020 to 2040 against the time zone database found no difference. The hour that does not exist in March and the hour that occurs twice in October are read as summer time.

25	
26	## What I found in the appointments web pages
27	
28	| Finding | Action |
29	|---|---|
30	| The BFF always returns 200, so a 409 looks like success | The BFF forwards the status code of the API (`fix`) |
31	| `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_KEY` ships the API key to the browser | The API URL and the key come from server-only environment variables |
32	| The Overview page calls the API directly | The Overview page calls a new BFF summary route |
33	| The create form closes whatever the result | The form shows the error and stays open (`fix`) |
34	| The status filter sends `canceled`, so it shows only legacy appointments | The filter sends `cancelled` (`fix`) |
35	| Times display in browser time, and the form reads the start time as browser time | Times display in venue time (Europe/Berlin), and the form reads the start time as venue time (`fix`) |
36	| The BFF sends any body and any id to the API, so `..%2Fcustomers` as an id reaches another API route | The appointment BFF handlers parse the body with the contract and accept digits only as an id |

38	## What did you skip, and why?
39	
40	- **The BFF handlers of customers and treatments.** They still answer 200 for each API status. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
41	- **The same rule for a special hour in the form and in legacy data.** In the hour that occurs twice in October, the form reads winter time and a legacy appointment reads summer time. 42	- **The log of the customer request body.** `POST /customers` still prints the name, the email and the phone. The brief limits the work to appointments.
43	- **An edit form for a staff member.** The API and the BFF can change one, and the page only lists and creates. The brief asks for a list page and a create form.
44	- **A rollout plan for the new list contract.** `GET /appointments` changes its response shape and drops `date` in one release. 45	- **Error bodies of customers and treatments.** They keep their four shapes. The brief limits the refactor to appointments.
46	- **Signed links for the confirmation page.** Appointment ids are sequential, so anyone can read a booking by its id. The page now gets only the id, the customer name, the treatment name and duration, the start and end time, the price and the status.
47	- **A browser check of the list controls.** The URL state has no automated test. I checked the production build, the page with a full query string, and the BFF answers. I did not click the controls in a browser.

49	- **The same error order in the BFF and the API.** For an unknown id with an invalid body, `PATCH` answers 400 in the BFF and 404 in the API, because the BFF parses the body first.
50	- **Authentication in the web app.** The staff BFF route `/api/appointments/:id` still returns `notes` to anyone who has the URL. The confirmation page no longer calls it.
51	- **An outbox for reminders.** A crash between the claim and the send loses one reminder. So does a send that the email provider rejects, because the job does not retry.
52	- **A two-release rollout for soft delete.** During a rolling update, the previous version still shows a deleted appointment and still counts it in the overlap check. See `docs/migrations.md`.
53	- **A data migration for legacy start times.** The stored values stay as they are. A rewrite of customer data cannot be rolled back.
54	- **The SQL injection in `GET /customers?search=`.** The route still builds its SQL from the `search` value with `sql.raw`. The brief limits the work to appointments. This is the first fix before the API goes live.

56	- **A new reminder for a moved appointment.** A change of the start time keeps the reminder mark. An appointment that moves after its reminder gets no reminder for the new time. No test covers this. A fix clears the mark when the start time changes.

59	## Behaviour that changed outside a `fix` commit
60	
61	The appointments refactor keeps the status code and the body for each valid input. These responses to invalid input changed:
62	
63	| Input | Before | After |
64	|---|---|---|
65	| SQL in the `status` or `date` filter | 200 with all appointments, or 500 | 200 with an empty list |
66	| A filter sent twice (`?status=a&status=b`) | 200 with an empty list | 400 |
67	| `customerId` or `treatmentId` that is not a positive integer (`-1`, `1.5`, `"1"`, `[1]`, `true`) | 201, 404 or 500 | 400 |
68	| `notes` that is not a string or `null` | accepted, or 500 | 400 |
69	| An appointment whose customer or treatment row is missing (the seed has none; I wrote two to the database by hand) | 200 with a partial item, or 500 | absent from the list, 404 on read and update; the summary still counts it |
70	| The reminder job meets an appointment whose customer row is missing | The job throws, and sends no later reminder in that run | The job skips that appointment |

72	**Error bodies changed too**, in the `refactor` commits `a99548f` and `94a22e4`. The README says that an error body is not part of the contract. 74	Three more changes have no effect on a response:
75	
76	- **The in-memory booking lock is gone.** The service is now synchronous, so one process cannot interleave two bookings. The rule across replicas is a separate fix.
77	- **A booking is one insert with the real price.** Before, it was an insert with price 0 and then an update.
78	- **No log line prints an appointment request body.** The refactor commit `94a22e4` removed it.
79	
80	## Characterization tests that changed
81	
82	Each change is its own commit. Three commits touch the folder `apps/api/test/characterization`.
83	
84	| Test | Before | After | Reason | Commit |
85	|---|---|---|---|---|
86	| `POST /appointments` "an appointment that starts as another one ends" | 409 | 201 | The README says back-to-back is fine. The test recorded a bug. | `c7c9db5`; the fix is `b59a55a` |
87	| The six `GET /appointments` tests ("returns every appointment with its customer and treatment", "orders ISO-timestamped appointments by start time", "computes endsAt from the treatment duration", "filters by status", "filters by date", "combines the status and date filters") | They read an array and use `?date=` | They read `items` and use `?from=&to=`; two also check `total` | The brief replaces the list contract. 88	| The helper `helpers/server.ts` | No `delete` method | A `delete` method | The tests of `DELETE /appointments/:id` need it. No test in the folder changed. | `174428b` |
89	
90	The test changes first, so the suite is red at `c7c9db5` (one test) and at `7ea5fdc` (six tests). The next commit makes it green.

95	
96	The brief forbids a rewrite of the history, so these stay. 98	| Commit | What is wrong |
99	|---|---|
100	| `f75dd8a`, `a99548f` | `yarn install --immutable` fails. `yarn.lock` already lists the contract package for the web app, and `apps/web/package.json` gets it only in `211698d`. A normal install works. |

103	| `769901a`, `ff7f535` | Each holds more than one fix. |
104	| `2f3f152`, `bca1a4f`, `8c14178`, `ff7f535`, `3ebe0be`, `5f2cd7c`, `89ab2fd` | `fix` commits with no test: five change the web app, one changes a message of `db:check`, and one changes the web Dockerfile. I checked the last one with a build and a run of both images. |

108	Five of seven checks pass: both typechecks, jscpd, `db:check` and the tests. Two fail, and each finding is in code that came with the repo. I left that code as it is, because the brief limits the work to appointments.
109	
110	| Check | Finding | Where |
111	|---|---|---|
112	| ESLint | 18 errors: `any`, and two unused `reply` parameters | `apps/api/src/routes.ts`, the customers and treatments routes |
113	| ESLint | 1 error: `any` | `apps/web/app/treatments/page.tsx` |
114	| knip | The unused file `apps/api/src/utils/legacy.ts` | Its own comment says that nothing imports it |
115	| knip | The unused packages `lodash`, `@types/lodash` and `dayjs` | The two `package.json` files |
116

118
