121	## Where did the AI get something wrong, and how did you catch it?
122	
123	- **Legacy `startsAt` in responses.** The AI first advised to return it as stored, to keep "today's shape". A second read of the README rule and of the ordering test, which skips legacy rows, showed that normalisation is correct.
124	
125	- **Staff order without regard to letter case.** The AI ordered `GET /staff` with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The brief says "ordered by name", and its tests run against that contract. A review flagged the addition, and the plain order replaced it.
126	
127	- **Loose ids in the routes.** The AI read each path id with `Number`, as the original code did. A review probed `DELETE /appointments/1e0`, and it deleted appointment 1. The routes now read the id with the id schema of the contract, and tests cover `1e0`, `0x1` and `1.0`.
128	
129	- **Staff email in lower case.** The AI-written plan stored the email in lower case. A response would then differ from the input. The index on `lower(email)` gives the same uniqueness and keeps the value.
130	
131	Each ticket ended with a review by a second agent that had not seen the work, and I probed the result with real requests. These came out of that:
132	
133	| Mistake of the AI | How it was caught | Result |
134	|---|---|---|
135	| After the overlap fix, a `PATCH` could set a cancelled appointment back to `confirmed` on top of a later booking, with no overlap check. | The review of the overlap fix | "Cancelling is final" (`50eb8c1`) closes it, with a test |

137	| The list read the page and the total in two reads, so a write of another replica could make them disagree. Equal values kept ascending ids in a `desc` sort. | The review of the list | `769901a` |
138	| A `DELETE` with a JSON content type and no body returned 400. | A request by hand after the review | `18a3980` |

140	| The API client of the web app was server-only in name. Nothing stopped an import from a browser component. | The review of the web refactor | The `server-only` package, before the commit |
141	| The decision record of the reminder said that a reminder is lost "only on a crash". A rejected send loses it too. The first `docs/migrations.md` said that each migration only adds. | A check of each sentence against the code | The record changed before its commit; `492dbb7` |
142	| A reviewer agent said that the previous API version gets `SQLITE_BUSY` at once during a booking. | I read the driver: `better-sqlite3` waits 5 seconds by default | The claim did not go into the documents |
143	| The AI rewrote the error classes as functions after a remark of mine, and it put a new test file in the characterization folder. | I read each diff before the commit | Both reverted. A remark is not an instruction, and new tests go outside that folder |
144	
145	## What would you do next with another day?
146	
147	- **i18n.** The pages and the error messages hold English text in the code.
148	- **Import aliases.** The web handlers use paths such as `../../../../../lib/api`. An alias such as `@/lib/api` removes them.
149	- **oxlint and oxfmt in place of ESLint.** They run faster, so each check in the edit loop costs less. The repo has no formatter today.
150	- **Husky with pre-commit hooks.** Lint, typecheck and `db:check` run before each commit, not only in `yarn verify`.
151	- **CASL, if the app gets roles.** Today each caller with the API key can do all actions. With roles, one set of ability rules serves the API and the pages.
152	- **`@fastify/error` in place of the custom error classes.** It gives each error a code and a status in the way Fastify expects.
153	
154	## What would you want in place before this goes live?
155	
156	- A database that is not one SQLite file. The booking transaction takes the write lock of the whole database, a replica that waits for it blocks its event loop for up to 5 seconds and then returns 500, and WAL mode needs all replicas on one host.
157	
158	- Foreign keys, indexes and constraints on the three original tables.
159	- Mandatory authentication, and a CORS setting that is not `*`.
160	- Money as integer cents, not `REAL`.
161	- A readiness check that fails when the schema is behind the code, so the platform sends no request to that replica.
162	- A guard on `db:seed`. The script is in the production image, and it replaces all data. It has no guard, because the tests of the brief run it and I do not know their `NODE_ENV`.
163	- A pinned base image (a digest in place of `node:22-slim`), and a volume that Kubernetes mounts with the right owner.
164	- A clean stop for the web image. The Next server exits on `SIGTERM` with code 143 and does not wait for an open request.
165	- A structured logger. The Fastify logger is off, so an unexpected 500 leaves no log line today.
166	- An outbox with retry for reminders.
167	- Signed links for the customer confirmation page.
168	- A compile step for the API image.

- **Only a change away from `cancelled` is blocked (409).** The README says an appointment "normally" goes pending → confirmed → completed, which is not a rule.

The claim also requires the status `confirmed`, so an appointment cancelled a moment before gets no reminder. Two more fixes came with the first test of the job. It read a legacy start time as server time, so on a server that runs in UTC the 24 hour window was off by the venue offset. The email also stated the start time in server time.
- **The confirmation page gets its own BFF route with a public schema.** The API keeps `notes` for staff. The BFF is the boundary to the customer.
- **The delete button is on the appointment list.** No appointment detail page exists.
- **A new `startsAt` must be ISO 8601 with `Z` or an offset, and is stored as UTC.** A string without a zone has no defined instant.
- **Staff email is stored as sent, with a unique index on `lower(email)`.** The response then equals the input, and `Anna@x.com` still conflicts with `anna@x.com`. The index rejects the duplicate, so two replicas cannot both insert it. `GET /staff` uses the plain order of the database, so `Zoe` comes before `anna`; the brief says only "ordered by name". The check uses the same command as `db:generate`, so the two cannot disagree. - **The error body of the API key check.** A request with no key or a wrong key gets 401 with `{ error: 'Unauthorized' }`. The check came with the repo and answers in a hook, so the error handler does not make this body. The contract has no code for it. My plan did not cover it.
- **A new reminder for a moved appointment.** A change of the start time keeps the reminder mark. An appointment that moves after its reminder gets no reminder for the new time. No test covers this. A fix clears the mark when the start time changes.
- **The customer cache of the appointments page.** The module-level `customerCache` came with the repo and nothing clears it. A customer that is created after the first load is absent from the create form until a reload. A status change that the API rejects also shows no message; the list only loads again.

## Behaviour that changed outside a `fix` commit

The appointments refactor keeps the status code and the body for each valid input. A differential run sent the same 151 requests to the code before the refactor (`4a4f10d`) and after it (`94a22e4`) to check this. I ran it again at the end, with the same result. These responses to invalid input changed:

| Input | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| SQL in the `status` or `date` filter | 200 with all appointments, or 500 | 200 with an empty list |
| A filter sent twice (`?status=a&status=b`) | 200 with an empty list | 400 |
| `customerId` or `treatmentId` that is not a positive integer (`-1`, `1.5`, `"1"`, `[1]`, `true`) | 201, 404 or 500 | 400 |
| `notes` that is not a string or `null` | accepted, or 500 | 400 |
| An appointment whose customer or treatment row is missing (the seed has none; I wrote two to the database by hand) | 200 with a partial item, or 500 | absent from the list, 404 on read and update; the summary still counts it |
| The reminder job meets an appointment whose customer row is missing | The job throws, and sends no later reminder in that run | The job skips that appointment |

**Error bodies changed too**, in the `refactor` commits `a99548f` and `94a22e4`. The README says that an error body is not part of the contract. Each appointment error now has the body `{ error: { code, message, details? } }`. The same handler changes three error bodies on all routes, customers and treatments included, and keeps the status code: a malformed JSON body (400), an unknown route (404) and an unexpected error (500). The 500 body no longer shows the text of the SQL error.

Three more changes have no effect on a response:

- **The in-memory booking lock is gone.** The service is now synchronous, so one process cannot interleave two bookings. The rule across replicas is a separate fix.
- **A booking is one insert with the real price.** Before, it was an insert with price 0 and then an update.
- **No log line prints an appointment request body.** The refactor commit `94a22e4` removed it.

## Characterization tests that changed

Each change is its own commit. Three commits touch the folder `apps/api/test/characterization`.

| Test | Before | After | Reason | Commit |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `POST /appointments` "an appointment that starts as another one ends" | 409 | 201 | The README says back-to-back is fine. The test recorded a bug. | `c7c9db5`; the fix is `b59a55a` |
| The six `GET /appointments` tests ("returns every appointment with its customer and treatment", "orders ISO-timestamped appointments by start time", "computes endsAt from the treatment duration", "filters by status", "filters by date", "combines the status and date filters") | They read an array and use `?date=` | They read `items` and use `?from=&to=`; two also check `total` | The brief replaces the list contract. The expected appointments are the same. | `7ea5fdc`; the feature is `a07f3a1` |
| The helper `helpers/server.ts` | No `delete` method | A `delete` method | The tests of `DELETE /appointments/:id` need it. No test in the folder changed. | `174428b` |

The test changes first, so the suite is red at `c7c9db5` (one test) and at `7ea5fdc` (six tests). The next commit makes it green.

`apps/api/test/appointments-edges.test.ts` is my own file, and it also records behaviour that the refactor had to keep. Two of its tests recorded a bug and changed in the same way: `76c175c` (the legacy status) and `7b13069` (the legacy start time). My other tests that read the list changed inside the feature commit `a07f3a1`.

## What is wrong in the commit history

The brief forbids a rewrite of the history, so these stay. A script checked out each `refactor` and `fix` commit in a clone, and ran the tests at the commit and on its parent. `yarn test` is green at 9 of the 10 `refactor` commits. Of the 26 `fix` commits, 19 have an API test, and 18 of those tests fail on the parent.

| Commit | What is wrong |
|---|---|
| `f75dd8a`, `a99548f` | `yarn install --immutable` fails. `yarn.lock` already lists the contract package for the web app, and `apps/web/package.json` gets it only in `211698d`. A normal install works. |
| `f75dd8a` | One new test in `contract.test.ts` is red, because it expects the error body that the next commit adds. The characterization suite is green. |
| `17aec28` | A `fix` commit whose test also passes on the parent. It removes the staff order without regard to letter case. |
| `769901a`, `ff7f535` | Each holds more than one fix. |
| `2f3f152`, `bca1a4f`, `8c14178`, `ff7f535`, `3ebe0be`, `5f2cd7c`, `89ab2fd` | `fix` commits with no test: five change the web app, one changes a message of `db:check`, and one changes the web Dockerfile. I checked the last one with a build and a run of both images. |

## What `yarn verify` still reports

Five of seven checks pass: both typechecks, jscpd, `db:check` and the tests. Two fail, and each finding is in code that came with the repo. I left that code as it is, because the brief limits the work to appointments.

| Check | Finding | Where |
|---|---|---|
| ESLint | 18 errors: `any`, and two unused `reply` parameters | `apps/api/src/routes.ts`, the customers and treatments routes |
| ESLint | 1 error: `any` | `apps/web/app/treatments/page.tsx` |
| knip | The unused file `apps/api/src/utils/legacy.ts` | Its own comment says that nothing imports it |
| knip | The unused packages `lodash`, `@types/lodash` and `dayjs` | The two `package.json` files |

ESLint also prints 10 warnings: nine `console` statements and one hook dependency in the customers page. One `console` statement is mine, the log of a failed shutdown in `apps/api/src/index.ts`. The others came with the repo.

The appointments module, the staff module, the contract package and the tests have no ESLint error and no warning. The mapper has its own `toStatus` and does not use `legacyStatus` from the unused file, because that one returns a plain `string` and not the status type of the contract.

## Where did the AI get something wrong, and how did you catch it?

- **Legacy `startsAt` in responses.** The AI first advised to return it as stored, to keep "today's shape". A second read of the README rule and of the ordering test, which skips legacy rows, showed that normalisation is correct.

- **Staff order without regard to letter case.** The AI ordered `GET /staff` with `COLLATE NOCASE`. The brief says "ordered by name", and its tests run against that contract. A review flagged the addition, and the plain order replaced it.

- **Loose ids in the routes.** The AI read each path id with `Number`, as the original code did. A review probed `DELETE /appointments/1e0`, and it deleted appointment 1. The routes now read the id with the id schema of the contract, and tests cover `1e0`, `0x1` and `1.0`.

- **Staff email in lower case.** The AI-written plan stored the email in lower case. A response would then differ from the input. The index on `lower(email)` gives the same uniqueness and keeps the value.

Each ticket ended with a review by a second agent that had not seen the work, and I probed the result with real requests. These came out of that:

| Mistake of the AI | How it was caught | Result |
|---|---|---|
| After the overlap fix, a `PATCH` could set a cancelled appointment back to `confirmed` on top of a later booking, with no overlap check. | The review of the overlap fix | "Cancelling is final" (`50eb8c1`) closes it, with a test |
| `PATCH {"status":"cancelled"}` on a legacy appointment rewrote the stored `canceled`, although the response showed no change. | The review of the status fix | The service writes only a value that differs from the one the API shows |
| The list read the page and the total in two reads, so a write of another replica could make them disagree. Equal values kept ascending ids in a `desc` sort. | The review of the list | `769901a` |
| A `DELETE` with a JSON content type and no body returned 400. | A request by hand after the review | `18a3980` |
| An injection test passed on the old code too. The first test of the `canceled` migration ran the fix on an empty table. | The question "does it fail without the change?" in two reviews | The first changed before its commit; the second is `79acf95` |
| The API client of the web app was server-only in name. Nothing stopped an import from a browser component. | The review of the web refactor | The `server-only` package, before the commit |
| The decision record of the reminder said that a reminder is lost "only on a crash". A rejected send loses it too. The first `docs/migrations.md` said that each migration only adds. | A check of each sentence against the code | The record changed before its commit; `492dbb7` |
| A reviewer agent said that the previous API version gets `SQLITE_BUSY` at once during a booking. | I read the driver: `better-sqlite3` waits 5 seconds by default | The claim did not go into the documents |
| The AI rewrote the error classes as functions after a remark of mine, and it put a new test file in the characterization folder. | I read each diff before the commit | Both reverted. A remark is not an instruction, and new tests go outside that folder |

## What would you do next with another day?

- **i18n.** The pages and the error messages hold English text in the code.
- **Import aliases.** The web handlers use paths such as `../../../../../lib/api`. An alias such as `@/lib/api` removes them.
- **oxlint and oxfmt in place of ESLint.** They run faster, so each check in the edit loop costs less. The repo has no formatter today.
- **Husky with pre-commit hooks.** Lint, typecheck and `db:check` run before each commit, not only in `yarn verify`.
- **CASL, if the app gets roles.** Today each caller with the API key can do all actions. With roles, one set of ability rules serves the API and the pages.
- **`@fastify/error` in place of the custom error classes.** It gives each error a code and a status in the way Fastify expects.

## What would you want in place before this goes live?

- A database that is not one SQLite file. The booking transaction takes the write lock of the whole database, a replica that waits for it blocks its event loop for up to 5 seconds and then returns 500, and WAL mode needs all replicas on one host.

- Foreign keys, indexes and constraints on the three original tables.
- Mandatory authentication, and a CORS setting that is not `*`.
- Money as integer cents, not `REAL`.
- A readiness check that fails when the schema is behind the code, so the platform sends no request to that replica.
- A guard on `db:seed`. The script is in the production image, and it replaces all data. It has no guard, because the tests of the brief run it and I do not know their `NODE_ENV`.
- A pinned base image (a digest in place of `node:22-slim`), and a volume that Kubernetes mounts with the right owner.
- A clean stop for the web image. The Next server exits on `SIGTERM` with code 143 and does not wait for an open request.
- A structured logger. The Fastify logger is off, so an unexpected 500 leaves no log line today.
- An outbox with retry for reminders.
- Signed links for the customer confirmation page.
- A compile step for the API image.

---
name: colima-build-vm
description: Docker on this machine runs in colima; the default 2 GiB VM cannot build the web image, and `colima delete` keeps data without --data
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Docker on this machine runs in colima. The `default` profile has 2 GiB and is usually stopped.

- The web image of the Treatwell take-home does not build in 2 GiB: `yarn workspaces focus @venue/web` is killed for lack of memory. It builds in 4 GiB.
- Use a temporary profile: `colima start --profile venue-build --memory 4 --cpu 2`. Docker then points to it.
- `colima delete --profile <name> --force` keeps the containers, images and volumes of the profile. Add `--data` to remove them. (Found on 2026-10-11: a profile "deleted" earlier still held its containers.)
- Compound commands with `docker rm` or `docker volume rm` were denied in this project. Give containers new names instead, and remove the whole temporary profile at the end.

- Use a temporary profile: `colima start --profile venue-build --memory 4 --cpu 2`. Docker then points to it.
- `colima delete --profile <name> --force` keeps the containers, images and volumes of the profile. Add `--data` to remove them. (Found on 2026-10-11: a profile "deleted" earlier still held its containers.)
- Compound commands with `docker rm` or `docker volume rm` were denied in this project. Give containers new names instead, and remove the whole temporary profile at the end.

#!/bin/bash
# Loads each page and each BFF route of the copy that runs with `yarn dev` in the container.
# Host port 3100 is the web app, host port 4100 is the API.
OUT="$(dirname "$0")/p.out"
q() { curl -s -o "$OUT" -w "%{http_code}" --max-time 60 "$@"; }

echo "--- pages"
for u in / /appointments "/appointments?status=cancelled&sortBy=price&sortDir=desc&pageSize=5&page=1" /customers /treatments /staff /appointments/1/confirmation /nope; do
  code=$(q "localhost:3100$u")
  echo "[$code] $u  bytes=$(wc -c < "$OUT" | tr -d ' ')  nav=$(grep -c 'Venue Backoffice' "$OUT")  staff-link=$(grep -c 'href="/staff"' "$OUT")"
done

echo "--- BFF"
for u in /api/appointments "/api/appointments?status=cancelled&pageSize=2" /api/appointments/summary /api/appointments/1 /api/appointments/1/confirmation /api/customers /api/treatments /api/staff "/api/appointments?date=2026-10-05" /api/appointments/abc; do
  code=$(q "localhost:3100$u")
  echo "[$code] $u  $(cut -c1-110 "$OUT")"
done

echo "--- writes through the BFF"
echo "[$(q -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"name":"Anna Vogel","email":"anna@example.com"}' localhost:3100/api/staff)] POST /api/staff $(cut -c1-100 "$OUT")"
echo "[$(q -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"customerId":1,"treatmentId":1,"startsAt":"2026-10-05T09:30:00Z"}' localhost:3100/api/appointments)] POST an overlap $(cut -c1-110 "$OUT")"
echo "[$(q -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"customerId":8,"treatmentId":2,"startsAt":"2026-11-10T09:00:00Z"}' localhost:3100/api/appointments)] POST a free time $(cut -c1-60 "$OUT")"
echo "[$(q -X DELETE localhost:3100/api/appointments/15)] DELETE 15"
echo "[$(q localhost:3100/api/appointments/15)] GET 15 after the delete"

echo "--- API directly"
echo "[$(q localhost:4100/health)] /health $(cat "$OUT")"
echo "[$(q localhost:4100/appointments/15/audit)] audit of 15 $(cut -c1-60 "$OUT")"

echo "--- lines of the dev log with an error, or a request that is not 2xx"
docker exec fresh sh -c 'grep -i -E "error|failed|⨯" /tmp/dev.log | head -8' | cut -c1-200
docker exec fresh sh -c 'grep -E "^ (GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE) " /tmp/dev.log | grep -v -E " (200|201|204) in " | head -10' | cut -c1-160

Ticket 24 is done: all four criteria hold at `21ec1a5`. All 24 tickets now have the status `done`. This ticket changed no code, so there is no commit and I ran no review agent.

## Results

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `yarn verify` in a fresh clone | 5 of 7 pass, the same as in your repo. `NOTES.md` names each red finding. |
| `db:migrate` → `db:seed` → `start` in a fresh clone | The API works: reads, a create, the audit trail and a delete. |
| `yarn dev` from the committed files, with the README steps | Each of the six pages answers 200, each BFF route returns data, and a create, a 409 and a delete work through the BFF. |
| The history | 76 commits, no merge. The reflog holds one clone and 75 commits: no amend, no rebase, no reset. A commit changes 43 lines in the median. |
| Both Docker images | They build at the final commit and report `healthy` together. |

Two limits of the `yarn dev` check:

- Your dev server holds ports 3000 and 4000, so I ran the fresh copy in a clean Node 22 container on other ports.
- The check is by HTTP. It does not run the page code of a browser, so your click-through still counts.

## One finding

With two CPU cores, `yarn dev` starts only the API. `yarn workspaces foreach --parallel` runs about half as many jobs as the machine has cores, and each `dev` script runs without end. With four cores both apps start.

The root `dev` script came with the repo, so I only added the finding to `NOTES.md`, as you chose for the legacy lint findings. The fix is one flag, `--jobs unlimited`. I recommend it, because the brief says `yarn dev` must work from a fresh clone and a reviewer can use a small VM. Tell me if you want it; it is one `fix` commit.

1. **Do not push to `origin` without a check.** `origin` is `Treatwell-AI/ai-engineer-take-home`, and `origin/main` is still the initial commit. The 75 commits and the three tags are local. Push there only if Treatwell said that repo is yours.

4. **The tag `phase-3-ship`** goes on the last commit, after those commits.

content.content:
## Traps for later phases

1. **Seed runs after migrate.** The reviewers run `db:migrate`, `db:seed`, `start`. The seed puts `canceled` and legacy dates back after the fix migration. Reads must still normalise them, or the seed must change.
2. **Synchronous transactions.** `better-sqlite3` transactions cannot take an async callback. Audit "in the same transaction" must use synchronous Drizzle calls. AI tools often get this wrong.
3. **Sorting and Berlin date filters.** Mixed `startsAt` formats sort wrongly as text. The API has no time zone library. Pagination needs an `id` tiebreak to be stable.
4. **Test helper.** `helpers/server.ts` has no `delete` method. The new list shape breaks all six `GET /appointments` tests.
5. **Rolling update.** The old API version ignores a new `deletedAt` column, so it shows deleted rows during rollout. This belongs in `docs/migrations.md`.
6. **Production start.** `start` uses `tsx`, which is a devDependency. This matters for the Dockerfile because the script name must stay.
7. **Staff email.** Case-insensitive uniqueness needs an expression index on `lower(email)`. It is not confirmed that `drizzle-kit generate` emits it correctly.
8. **Reminder job.** It must skip soft-deleted appointments.

## Open questions for the reviewers

- There is no appointment detail page, only the list and the confirmation page. Where does the delete button go?
- Does an unknown query parameter, such as the old `date`, return 400, or is it ignored?
- "Items keep today's shape" conflicts with "the API uses ISO 8601" for the epoch `createdAt` and the legacy `startsAt` strings. Which one wins?
=== plan: steps 4 and verification
   - Postgres differences: advisory lock around migrate, `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`, lock timeouts, batched data fixes, exclusion constraint for overlaps, `AT TIME ZONE` in place of the hand-written daylight-saving rule.

## Step 4 — notes and submission

`NOTES.md`, one page, answers the five questions in the brief. Fill it from real events during the work: decisions, skipped items, AI mistakes and how they were caught, next steps, pre-launch needs. The draft already holds the decisions from the grilling session. Check each line against the commits, and cut it to one page.

## Verification

- `yarn test` after each commit in Steps 1 and 1b.
- `yarn verify` at the end of each step. List what still fails and why.
- Fresh-clone check: delete `apps/api/data`, run `yarn dev`, open the four pages plus staff.
- Production check: `NODE_ENV=production yarn workspace @venue/api start` against an empty database must not create tables.
- Run `yarn db:migrate` twice. The second run must change nothing.
- Change `schema.ts` without a migration. `yarn db:check` must fail. Revert.
- `docker build` both images. Run the API image with `db:migrate` then `start`.
- Manual `curl` for each new status code in the brief (staff 400/404/409, list 400, delete 204/404, audit 404).

No. Leave it out.

- **It is a generated file.** `next dev` writes it with paths to `.next/dev/types/`, and `next typegen` (which `yarn verify` runs) writes it back with `.next/types/`. The committed version is the one from the starting repo.
- **A commit of it adds noise.** The diff would show a change to a file that is not part of your work, and the file flips again the next time someone runs the other command.
- **It does not affect the push.** A push sends only commits, so an uncommitted change stays on your machine.

To clear it from `git status`, stop the dev server and run:

```bash
git restore apps/web/next-env.d.ts
```

`yarn verify` also puts it back.
